speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head X of the Estimates be reduced by $100".

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Mr Chairman, I thought long and hard about what to raise in my very first kick-off speech as Chair of the MCCY GPC.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We focused a large part of our post-Independence nation-building years on our infrastructure, growing our economy and securing jobs for the future, and rightly so.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But if these issues represent the physical body of our nation, then issues on Culture, Community, Youth & Sports must surely represent our soul, the heartbeat of our social consciousness, and our collective dreams and aspirations as a nation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: My takeaway from GE 2020 is a strong desire among Singaporeans, especially our youths, to be actively engaged in wanting to be part of the conversation to shape and mould our future together.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: And this forms the context of the exciting and inspiring work that lies ahead for the MCCY team as we start this term of Government.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: And while they embraced the English language as the official and working language in Singapore, my brothers and I were inculcated to always remember our cultural roots.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: But what fascinates me most, as I remember my growing up years, was how we evolved parts of the Chinese culture into what is uniquely Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I have spoken about this before in Parliament. “新谣” or Chinese ballads produced by young Singaporeans and the local Chinese film productions are good examples.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I shall elaborate more on this in another MCCY cut later.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Sports can inspire and unite a nation regardless of the diversity of its people.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: My inspiration from sports, in my youth, however, was drawn particularly from football.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Now, more a spectator than a player, football was something I enjoyed playing and followed closely in my youth.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Part of the reason for that was the local football scene at the time.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I was just born when Singapore won the Malaysia Cup in 1964.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: We also won the trophy when I was a teenager in 1977.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: I am sure many of us recollect the many exciting Malaysia Cup matches in the early 1990s when the Kallang Roar reverberated the old stadium.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: V Sundramoorthy’s bicycle kick against Brunei and Fandi Ahmad leading us to Malaysia Cup success in 1994 are memories, I believe, few Singaporeans of my generation will ever forget.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It would be a dream come through for us to qualify and, if we do, it will certainly inspire another entire generation of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is also about honoring the concept of level competition and being able to train and compete fairly, on equal terms and, more importantly, in a safe environment.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: So, in order for Sports to thrive in Singapore, providing a safe and positive environment for our athletes is crucial.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This is especially pertinent when it comes to our student athletes, who have invested much of their time and resources to pursue their passion in sports.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There have been well-documented reports of athlete abuse across all disciplines in many countries.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It must be recognised, however, that much work in this area has been done for sports in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In 2018, Sport Singapore (SportSG) launched the Safe Sport Commission.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: There are now well-trained Safeguarding Officers and well-thought through protocols that guide the coaches and trainers and provide adequate checks in the different sporting disciplines.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat, if you would like to take your two cuts together, please do.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, safe distancing measures have compelled Singapore residents of all faiths to adapt their religious practices.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With the limit placed on the number of congregants in the mosques, the online booking system has been useful to spread out the crowd and keep all attendees safe.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The upside of these additional space and barriers is that Muslim ladies can attend Friday prayers as well.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Where it has been impossible to obtain one of the coveted timeslots for Friday prayers at the mosques, many have turned to technology to carry on with their religious obligations, and tune in to sermons in the safety of their homes.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Web-based channels featuring Quran recitation guides and online courses on Islamic values have also proven beneficial for the young Muslims who could not attend the classes in person.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: With Ramadan just two months away, what are the plans for the special congregational tarawih prayers?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: (In Malay):   Mr Chairman, among the working population that has been negatively impacted by COVID-19, are our mature workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: The World Economic Forum revealed some significant findings in its latest Future of Jobs Report in October last year.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: We must ensure that our workers are able to leverage on new skills and capabilities to secure these new jobs and stay relevant.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Organisations like MENDAKI SENSE play a crucial role in equipping the community with relevant skills and knowledge to stay employable.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In recent years, in line with the national call to be future and digital ready, there has been growing emphasis to enhance our people's digital skills.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Digital and Data Literacy now sit among the main categories for professional development courses on MENDAKI SENSE's website.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: MENDAKI also has a series of Future Ready programmes which are popular among youth and young professionals in the community.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: However, I believe more can be done to help our older workers.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: In the past year, how have mature job seekers benefitted from professional development programmes with MENDAKI to progress in their careers and job search?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: How will MENDAKI and MENDAKI SENSE continue to ensure that the workforce within the Malay/Muslim community, specifically our mature workers, remain relevant and be future ready?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: This team comprised leaders from different sectors from the Government, businesses, community leaders, training providers, as well as the Labour Movement to brainstorm ideas and steer our community to face and overcome the challenges arising from the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Can the Minister share the progress of the team's efforts across the different levels of support, from workers, businesses as well as our community welfare groups?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: How can we continue to step up efforts to bridge the gaps so that our community can continue to receive assistance and also seize any opportunity to improve their lives?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: For jobseekers and potential employees, how can we help them to identify new skillsets that they need to pursue better job opportunities and better or lucrative wages?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: In addition, how can we continue to encourage young people who are ITE, polytechnics and universities graduates to place full-time employment as their main priority?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: They should only seek additional work such as food delivery when they have some free time to spare and are healthy enough.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: As far as possible, avoid using this kind of work, such as food delivery, as their main source of income because the returns are not holistic and there is no job security if they meet with an accident while doing deliveries.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Apart from the groups mentioned earlier, for madrasah students and religious teachers specifically, what are the efforts that can continue to help them can obtain job opportunities beyond teaching religious knowledge?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: My next request pertains to social support, that is, what can be done to strengthen our community’s financial and social capacity to continuously improve their lives?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: What are the outreach and support efforts that we can do for those who were left out or felt disappointed because their past requests and applications were rejected?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I am sure that many in our community have received social support from the Government while they were in school and later in life.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Such efforts can be a motivating factor for our children and youths.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: We are all aware of the community’s development and progress over the years, and so, what more can be done to ensure a consistent and better performance in the future?

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: Allow me to end my speech with a quatrain to motivate the Malay community and Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Abdul Samad (Nominated Member)
text: With a heart full of zeal and passion Defend our people and develop our nation Carry the hopes of our countrymen Build a community that is admired

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (In Malay):   Asatizah play an important role within the community to provide direction and guidance to the Muslim community.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: In Singapore, this is a critical responsibility as Muslims here live within the context of a multi-racial and multi-religious society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There are certain challenges faced by minorities living in a secular nation and society.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Among the issues that may have caused concern within the Muslim community in Singapore lately include matters related to same-sex relationships and the wearing of the tudung.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Sometimes complications arise because there are different thoughts and views in society on certain matters.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: We need to be sensitive to this situation and ensure that we do not disrupt and divide society, when we voice out our views.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Meaningful discussions require deep religious knowledge, maturity and an open mind from everyone involved.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The asatizah are able to shape the thoughts and attitudes of the Muslim community when addressing various issues by providing proper knowledge and developing a mature approach towards any particular issue.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: What is important is that the asatizah should continue to ensure that complex issues can be addressed, but at the same time, ensure that the harmony and well-being of the larger community are protected.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: There is Malay proverb that advises us to handle delicate issues carefully to avoid making things worse.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: (It is like removing a strand of hair from flour, the hair should not break, the flour should not scatter) Another source of new problems is the effects of the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Our community faces a multitude of social challenges related to employment, mental stress, marital problems and so on.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Religion can be a source of encouragement and strength for the Muslim community in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Therefore, asatizah must also be prepared to help address social issues and provide guidance to Muslims in this regard.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Last year, the report by the Committee on Future Asatizah (COFA) mentioned the importance of having future asatizah who fully understand and deeply comprehend the needs of the different communities.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: Indeed, a precise and deep understanding is important so that asatizah can really help the community emerge from difficult times, and stay positive and open-minded when facing problems.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: The asatizah need to have particular skills and this capability should be constantly improved.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
text: This is a very important programme to ensure that asatizah are given the necessary skills to carry out their responsibilities.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Please take your two cuts together, if you would like to.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: (In Malay):   With the disruptions brought about by COVID-19, our religious leadership played an important role in providing religious guidance to the community in getting through the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Moreover, this pandemic has accelerated the trend of learning new skills to keep up with changing needs, in terms of emerging industries and employment.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: For example, between July 2019 and June 2020, LinkedIn saw a 300% increase in total hours spent on LinkedIn Learning, compared to the year before.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: In essence, the pandemic provided many with the opportunity to upskill, acquiring new skills for the changing environment.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Given these developments, it is important to equip our asatizah with relevant skills to address complex issues.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: A key theme from the COFA conversations is the strong recognition that asatizah have a critical and essential role which they must continue to play, in guiding the community at all levels, contributing and galvanizing contributions to nation-building and humanity, as inspiring leaders, competent citizens, and effective contributors.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: There is also a need to strengthen the role of asatizah in nation-building.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: These can be done by strengthening asatizah’s core roles as religious leaders while leveraging opportunities for them to serve, contribute and develop themselves in adjacent areas, such as the social and education sector.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: More support and opportunities need to be given to overseas university students to upgrade their existing skill sets during their period of study.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Supporting our overseas undergraduates and postgraduates would nurture inspiring religious graduates and reinforce their commitment to constantly upgrade their skills.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Thus, Implementing these recommendations put forth by COFA also reaffirms our commitment to build up the asatizah sector, strengthening institutions, and seeing inspirational religious graduates.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: It is thus imperative that asatizah upskill to address the dynamic challenges of the future.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: As such, given the ongoing pandemic, what are the plans and programmes available to ensure that our asatizah are equipped with the relevant skills so that they can better serve the community?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: This teenager, was who was inspired by “far-right extremist ideology,” served as a reminder to Singaporeans that our religious harmony cannot be taken for granted.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: In 2019, an Australian gunman released a racist manifesto shortly before opening fire at two mosques in the city of Christchurch in New Zealand.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Given that globalisation has increased our connectedness with foreign cultures and communities, threats to our religious harmony in Singapore will continue to be challenged.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: It is thus imperative that we strengthen our harmony in Singapore by engendering interfaith understandings.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: It is also important that our local religious communities and asatizah stand firmly against radical ideologies and make clear that any copycat attacks will not find traction or support here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: (In Malay):   Sir, the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore, just like the rest of the country, is aware and concerned towards current issues that we face.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: It is the nature of Malays to help each other, as the Malay proverb goes – "shoulder any burden together".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: In preventing the spread of COVID-19, for instance, they have been swift in complying with all health measures, such as closing the mosques to curb any coronavirus infection here.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Although it was the only local newspaper report on the issue, some parties have said that the complaints against this individual have been raised a number of years ago.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My questions are: When was the first complaint received by MUIS about this individual who practice deviant teaching?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, why was further investigation only carried out after it was reported in the newspaper?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, what was the outcome of MUIS’ investigation so far?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Fourth, are the AMLA provisions sufficient or should it be reviewed and amended to strengthen its effectiveness in addressing deviant teachings?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The second issue is about allegations of possible misconduct in governance and abuse of power in the management of halal certificates.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: What was referred to CPIB if it is true that "MUIS' investigation does not find evidence" of corruption or abuse of power?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: As the Malays say, "a tree does not sway if there is no wind".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: New questions emerged after several reports over there linked Singapore and certain individuals from MUIS in this matter.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: I cite the following report: (In English): The Islamic Development Department (Jakim), does not discount the possibility that non-certified meat has been smuggled into the country and later sold as halal products.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Jakim Research Division, Senior Director, Datuk Dr Sirajuddin Suhaimee, in acknowledging this, said such cases had occurred in other countries.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Speaking in a special live interview via the Department's Facebook page, he said, "Jakim learned in a past forum that such cases has occurred in Singapore, because of this, Indonesia does not trust (halal) meat from Singapore.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: The non-certified meat reportedly entered the warehouse at the port and the packaging was changed, then stamped with a halal label.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: So, it is not impossible for this to happen in Malaysia today".

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, has MUIS conducted any investigation and who is leading the investigation, following the statement by Datuk Dr Sirajuddin?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, is it true that the individual linked to the viral picture in social media is the Assistant Director in MUIS' Halal Strategic Unit?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Fourth, is it true that he is now the Executive Director of the Mosque-Madrasah-Wakaf Shared Services?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: And if so, why has this individual been moved to a different role if no offence took place?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Fifth, in the investigation report by MUIS on 15 December 2020, MUIS made known its concern about leaked information in the form of emails, which it claims violate the Official Secrets Act.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: My questions are as follows: First, what is the amount of capital provided by Madrasah Irsyad to set up the Irsyad Trust Limited, which was originally called Irsyad Foundation Limited?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Second, what is the extent and jurisdiction of Madrasah Irsyad in the feasibility of setting up a subsidiary, in this regard, Irsyad Trust Limited?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Third, is it true that a Senior Director of Madrasah from MUIS has resigned in 2016, and then allowed to become CEO of Irsyad Trust Limited?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Four, what was the reason for the resignation of this Senior Director of Madrasah from MUIS?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Fifth, who approved his appointment as CEO of Irsyad Trust Limited?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Sixth question, where did Madrasah Irsyad obtain the capital that was used to create Irsyad Trust Limited?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Seven, I went to the three official websites of the Islamic Religious Council of Singapore, Madrasah Irsyad and Irsyad Trust Limited, and saw that none of them contained any declaration about their connection to one another, so can you explain why this is so?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
text: Eight, how does MUIS monitor, examine and perform "Checks and Balances" on Irsyad Trust Limited?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: (In Malay):   Mentoring is an important aspect of guiding the youths.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: One of the concerns I have relates to the guidance of high-risk Malay/Muslim youths who often come from families with many issues.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: They may have insufficient role models at home for a variety of reasons.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: It is not uncommon for such youths to suffer low confidence, poor performance in studies, or be involved in activities that may lead them down the road of juvenile delinquency.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
text: Such youths would benefit from a mentoring programme tailored to meet their complex situations under the ambit of M3.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, students, teachers and parents were all affected by the school closure during Circuit Breaker.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Many had to get used to home-based learning.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Despite the situation getting better, we do not know when this pandemic will end.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The mental health of our youth will be further tested with the increased risk of hacking cases and cyber-bullying and social media cases.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This April is the second time that our community will welcome the month of Ramadan amidst COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Previously, many in the community, including our youth, energized our mosques and social service organisations with volunteer activities during the whole of Ramadan.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: All of these changes and experiences may have a long-term effect on our youth.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It may not only cause stress and isolation tendencies, but also may shape the character of our entire youth generation.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Let us not allow our youth to feel alienated from the institutions of our community and their aspirations.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Here I would like to convey the desire of many Malay/Muslim youths who dream of a future where opportunities and employment is widely available for them based on their potential and capabilities; regardless of their lineage, beliefs or appearance.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: While we build our youth's capability to adapt and seize the opportunities in a post-pandemic world, we cannot lose sight in giving support and encouragement to them, be it in terms of education, character building or religion.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: This is for them to achieve their dreams and aspiration.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are MENDAKI's or M3's plans to support the aspirations of our youths so that they will continue to actively contribute to society?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: (In Malay):   When I was the Chairman of M3 at Chua Chu Kang, the KMM programme had a good response in terms of high enrolment.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: It teaches children not only numeracy skills but also equip parents with important learning techniques.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Learning requires an orderly, supportive and positive environment both within and outside the classroom.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: And the best predictor of student success is the involvement of parents.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: When parents are involved in their children's learning, the children show interest and better academic performance.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: How far has KMM helped in terms of teaching and parenting skills?

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: What are the efforts by Mendaki and M3 to continue equipping students and parents for an educational landscape that is quickly evolving?

speaker: The Chairman
text: If you wish to take your three cuts together, please do.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Yes, I would like to take my cuts; L, M and N together, please.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   COVID-19 has drastically impacted the lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: This is especially so for at-risk families, who require more support in terms of resources, learning tools, upskilling and gaining employment.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: During the circuit breaker, M3 and other Malay/Muslim organisations provided assistance particularly to at-risk families through programmes such as SGBukaPuasa.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we also ensure that those in need of support actually receive it?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   I would like to quote Minister Chan Chun Sing's speech that "COVID-19 is the crisis of our generation, but it can also be the opportunity of our generation." COVID-19 has changed our business and employment landscape.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Certain industries will decline while others, such as those in the digital economy or supporting the Green Plan, will see increased demand.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Disruptive technologies like driverless vehicles or drone deliveries, and our move towards electric vehicles, will render many present jobs redundant in affected industries.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Bridging sunset industries and emerging industries will be challenging.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Workers in affected industries may feel that the transfer of skills is not easy, but we must try nonetheless.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Digital skills and knowledge of the green economy will be integral to ensure that we remain relevant in the job market.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we increase awareness about the jobs available in these emerging industries among our community?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: As the Malay proverb goes, "Bend a bamboo while it is still a young bamboo shoot".

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How do we prepare our children and youth to have a passion for Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics so that our children can be prepared for the new economy?

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I recently spoke to a group of students from ITE College Central.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: They were excited to enter the job market, but some are worried about what they perceive to be discriminatory practices when looking for jobs and while working.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: We need to reassure our youths that there are existing laws that may be able to address some of their concerns.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Most importantly, we must continue to convince them that the best way to overcome this, is by deepening their capabilities in Digital or Green Technology that are needed by employers so that they can seize any available opportunity.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: (In Malay):   Last October, I presented the MENDAKI award to Muhammad Shafiq Akmal Bin Supri who topped his class in the Business Intelligence and Data Analytics diploma course in Temasek Polytechnic.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Shafiq, together with young professionals like Mr Amir Zakaria, a robotics engineer who is experienced in 3D-printing, are young trailblazers in our community and I wish them all the best for their pursuit to learn and subsequently embark on a career in the digital industry.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Can we initiate a network of mentors from the industries to help young people like them in their journey?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sharael Taha, I am afraid you have to wrap up.

speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
text: (In Malay):   Can the Minister provide an update on the Youth Mentoring Office and share some of the plans that it has implemented or will be implementing?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin, please take both your cuts together.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, since the COVID-19 outbreak, many activities and plans had to be postponed or cancelled, particularly for young couples who wish to get married.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: (In English): Marriage is a journey and it is important for couples to have a strong foundation, as they face many unknown stresses in transitioning to this new stage of life, for example, finances and family, work in care-giving.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: From first time newlyweds to reconstituted families, every relationship is different.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: But access to a listening ear and sound advice from trusted leaders is valuable.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As part of my work on the ground, I have encountered young women at different stages of their relationships.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Some were teen moms, some were struggling to find a job and others found it difficult to balance the responsibilities of a new wife.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I have had a newlywed write to me once when she opened up her heart on some of the identity issues she faced, after having a baby and becoming a stay-at-home mom.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Her email struck me as I realised that both she and I, had gotten married at about the same time.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In addition, due to the restrictions imposed due to COVID-19, how can the programme be better supported for online outreach, and given the diversity of the couples, is it possible to consider customisable modules to cater for the different needs and demographics of couples who may require more targeted support?

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And I hope that more in our community can participate, (In Malay):   I also support concerted efforts such as the "Ciptasama" programme which takes in views and engages the community to create the future that we want.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: However, in order to build and support the good efforts outlined under M3, I hope that more Malay/Muslim organisations will join forces with M3 agencies to pilot new ideas and have a deeper understanding of the community's concerns.

speaker: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And what roles can Malay/Muslim organizations play to enhance M3's efforts in reaching out and engaging our Malay/Muslim community more comprehensively, especially the Malay/Muslim women, since this is the year of Celebrating Singapore Women?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: It has been two years since M3 was established.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Since then, the M3 agencies have deepened their support for the community by collaborating with each other as well as the M3@Towns, and the programmes such as FITRAH, "Bersamamu" and the Youth Mentoring Office.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Our M3@Towns and professional groups have launched their own signature initiatives, such as our lawyer groups organising Legal Power of Attorney (LPA) sessions and setting up their own websites offering Pro-Bono legal services.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has seen M3 further work together and with other community partners like AMP, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry (SMCCI) and the Singapore Muslim Women's Association to quickly lend support to the community during this challenging time.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Yet, we must do even more to uplift our community if we are to close the gap on other communities but more importantly, to meet the aspirations of our own community.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: There are also some in the community who do not yet know what M3 even stands for.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: So, we must continue to find out new ways to be relevant, new ways to find out what is needed an what works, new ways of engaging.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Like any other organisation in today's world, M3 must continue to evolve its way of working.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Two necessary pillars must be one, digital and data and analytics, and two, partnerships.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How can M3 leverage digital and data to increase the effectiveness and impact of its initiatives?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Given our limited resources, how can M3 grow and strengthen its partnerships with other agencies, such as grassroots organisations, non-profit organisations and other organisations, both Malay/Muslim and non-Malay/Muslim, that can help us reach and help the members of the community who need us the most.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: (In Malay):   The Malay community has made a lot of progress.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We only have to look at the roaring business done at the many halal cafes at Kampung Glam.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: But when people feel left out, our sense of togetherness is affected and weakened.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: We do not want to we start creating divisions in our own community.

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: How can M3 be the glue to strengthen back that sense of togetherness of our community?

speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
text: Because our community's uniqueness is that we are taught from young to prepare for this world and the hereafter.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Mariam Jaafar, I am afraid you have to wrap up.

speaker: The Chairman
text: (In English): As we look forward to scale new heights as we emerge out of COVID-19, what more being done to enhance the M3 collaborations so that it remains relevant and impactful in meeting the needs of the community?

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Wan Rizal, if you would like to take your two cuts together, please do.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I welcome this move as it allows for better outreach to the community, especially in engaging the more vulnerable families within the towns.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: It also makes M³ programmes more accessible to the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am grateful because M³@Jalan Besar has the support of young and capable volunteers from various sectors.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: For instance, the come from the media, interfaith, education, social service, and public service sectors.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am heartened by the contributions and roles played by more young professionals when they help out as M3 volunteers.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Their contributions are critical to ensure that the outreach efforts of M³ are effective and sustainable.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Can the Minister provide an update on the plans to ensure that M³ volunteers are equipped with the relevant skills to reach out to the community more effectively?

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: (In Malay):   The Madrasah education system has come a long way.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I personally know many former madrasah students who are now notable alumni.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Other than producing reputable Muslim scholars, there are also madrasah graduates who are now business leaders, scientists, social science researchers, lawyers and many more.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: There are two Madrasah located in M³@Jalan Besar.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Recently, I visited Madrasah Aljunied to thank them for their success and congratulate them on passing the IB Programme.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I want to take this opportunity to congratulate the principal of Madrasah Aljunied, as well as the teachers and students for their success once again.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: The IB programme creates new pathways for madrasah students to non-religious opportunities.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: In this regard, the students should also be given exposure like attachments in various non-religious sectors.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, the past year has been challenging for every Singaporean, due to the disruptions caused by COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have come a long way from a year ago.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, I wish to put on record how proud I am to be part of the Malay/Muslim community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We made the necessary adjustments and rallied with our fellow Singaporeans, displaying a strong spirit of togetherness, regardless of race or religion to overcome this pandemic as a nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The difficult adjustments made by the community in response to COVID-19 was possible because our religious leadership was decisive and united.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS played a central role in this by issuing religious guidance early and rallying asatizah and mosque leaders to guide the community to adapt to the changing environment.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While MUIS was monitoring developments and decisions of religious authorities around the world, we could not simply copy what others had done, but rather had to find our own solutions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When difficult decisions were made, the community came together and supported these decisions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Everyone played a part to encourage and guide one another – lawyers, doctors, community leaders and ordinary citizens, all rolled up our sleeves.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The ability and confidence to chart our own path and make adjustments has allowed the Malay/Muslim community to thrive as a Community of Success, demonstrating the three Cs – Competence, Character and Citizenry.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why we must continue to invest in our asatizah and our community in these three fronts to strengthen our Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, we have to continue equipping our asatizah with the necessary competencies to deal with future challenges and confidently lead the community in a diverse and multi-religious nation like Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, we need to expand support for families, through which they develop our community's character.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And third, encourage active citizenry in our community so that we will always stand shoulder to shoulder with our fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to elaborate in Malay.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In Malay):   Chairman, last year, we saw how the COVID-19 pandemic transformed the situation in Singapore drastically.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The religious leadership in MUIS needed to play a critical role.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They worked with various parties in guiding the community to adapt to the evolving and challenging environment.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I was proud and heartened to see compassion in our community as we helped one another during these challenging times.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The religious leadership in MUIS were quick to consult health experts, and took in guidance from doctors, in guiding our community to adapt our socio-religious activities in overcoming the effects of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This initiative ensured continued support for zakat recipients and continued operations for our Malay/Muslim central kitchens, restaurants and delivery services.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, a group of Malay/Muslim lawyers, known as Lawyers@M3 came together to advise businesses on the new laws and regulations that were passed, and how this could help those affected by the Circuit Breaker measures, including home-based businesses.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The COVID-19 crisis also provided opportunities for our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It provided us with the opportunity to find innovative solutions to continue providing spiritual support for our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Moreover, we understood how our religious practices could adapt to avoid extended risks.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Clearly, we can be proud that we were able to adapt quickly and effectively.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS made sure that the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore continued to have access to the necessary spiritual support.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Mr Saktiandi highlighted, some of these solutions will become the new normal and continue beyond the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The streaming of sermons online, via MUIS' SalamSG channel on YouTube and Facebook will also continue.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These platforms have contributed to the wealth of high quality Islamic content available online.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Saktiandi's also asked about the congregational terawih prayers for the coming month of Ramadan, MUIS will share further details soon.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This clear and timely guidance also helped the community to face COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, it is in line with the strong values and principles in Islam, and has helped our community have full confidence to get the COVID-19 vaccine.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As religious leaders, asatizah bear the huge responsibility of providing guidance on religious matters, contextualised to Singapore's multi-cultural and multi-religious society, that is open and always facing rapid challenges.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Such guidance shapes our community’s character, so that we are able to overcome any future challenges and continue to thrive as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Rahayu Mahzam earlier asked what was done to ensure that asatizah are equipped with relevant skills.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We should evaluate the career of asatizah such that it is not different from other careers.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why, we must continue to train generations of asatizah who are ready for the future.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, we must build a lifelong learning ecosystem to enable them to continuously upgrade their skills and keep abreast of new developments.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The 1-year PCICS programme is a significant commitment and effort for our aspiring asatizah.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It also ensures that the achievements and skills of asatizah attained from various religious institutes of higher learning overseas are relevant and of quality to guide our religious lives that is suited to our multi-racial and multi-religious society and a rapidly changing world.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is important to maintain the standards of education to be recognised as a group of professionals.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To Mr Fahmi Aliman's query, under PCICS, students will be equipped with social work and counselling skills, in order to serve the local Malay/Muslim community more comprehensively.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will also enable asatizah to gain employment opportunities beyond the religious sector, as suggested by Mr Abdul Samad.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In response to Dr Wan Rizal's query, madrasahs provide a holistic education which includes both secular and religious subjects to develop religious thought leaders for the future who are confident in guiding a highly educated community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of the curriculum, madrasahs have introduced skills-based enrichment programmes and collaborated with various agencies to provide experiential learning journeys for students to gain exposure in the religious sector and beyond.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, Madrasah Al-Arabiah has embarked on a Science Research programme with the Institute of Bioengineering and Nanotechnology (IBN), A*Star and NUS.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Their students also participated in the CapitaLand Young Architects Programme.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: MUIS has been working with the mosque and madrasah sectors to implement the AWDP initiatives.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As part of AWDP, asatizah can look forward to the Skills Upgrading Programme and Career Competency Framework.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These programmes allow asatizah to equip themselves with relevant skills for the religious sector and adjacent sectors that would be beneficial for our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, to continue nurturing a Community of Success, we need to strengthen our Malay/Muslim families as a key building block of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A key area that requires attention is the changing needs of families.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Families are becoming more diverse – we have more inter-racial marriages, remarriages and complex family structures with step-parents and step-siblings.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin asked for an update on the "Bersamamu" programme.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under the "Bersamamu" programme, Kadi and Naib Kadi’s role is no longer limited to solemnising couples, but will also provide advice and support tailored to the couple prior to their marriage and for the first few years of their marriage.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This ensures that the couple can start their marriage on the right footing.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Apart from religious support, Kadi and Naib Kadi will also share information on national and community programmes that can benefit couples, such as such as KelasMateMatika@CC that is organised by M3 for pre-school children.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Nadia also asked about how "Bersamamu" can expand its online outreach efforts.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last January, the ROMM launched a Facebook page to help "Bersamamu" participants have easy access to information related to marriage, parenting and early childhood development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will provide couples with a useful resource and an opportunity to tap on the knowledge, experience and advice from fellow couples as well as the Kadi and Naib Kadi.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ROMM together with MUIS and MSF have started the Community of Practice Programme for Kadi and Naib Kadi.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The new programme provides Kadi and Naib Kadi the opportunity to interact and share experiences, and learn local and overseas best practices as part of Kadi and Naib Kadi's professional development.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, MSF is also refreshing the content for the "Cinta Abadi" marriage preparation course, to include the content such as the published fatwa on joint tenancy, so that families are equipped with relevant information.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The course is now offered online due to the COVID-19 safe management measures, and therefore allowing more couples to participate.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As we continue to nurture a Community of Success, we must also ensure that any assistance programmes remain accessible to the more vulnerable groups in our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: That is why the M3 initiative is central to the collaborations within the Malay/Muslim community and Minister Maliki Osman will elaborate on the future plans for M3 in his speech.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our community has also contributed to the Singapore Together Emerging Strong Conversations with two "Ciptasama@M3" sessions last January.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through these sessions, we listened to the views and suggestions from the community on both national and community issues that were of greatest concern to them.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Earlier this year, I announced that this year is the "Year of Celebrating SG Women".

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This speech is for all women in commemorating International Women’s Day today.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I hope through these conversations, we will gather ideas to support and celebrate the Malay/Muslim women in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Through these efforts, I hope that we can help to empower women, as well as build and strengthen a culture of active citenzry within our community and Singapore.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: (In English): Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap raised a few issues which I will attempt to answer during the clarification.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But for now, I would like to mention that to ensure that we live harmoniously in a diverse and multi-religious society, we have to make adjustments like other communities.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This adjustment that our community had to make over the last year to overcome the pandemic was not easy.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We stoically went through Ramadan without our prayers at mosques.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We could not even visit the graves of our loved ones.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our fellow Singaporeans too celebrated a muted Deepavali, Christmas and Chinese New Year recently.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We closed our mosques during the circuit breaker, as did churches and temples.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We were also one of the first countries to postpone the Haj pilgrimage last year – a major decision and others followed suit.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Come May, we will once again be celebrating Hari Raya – hopefully, with more spirit, but always ready to make adjustments so that we all stay safe.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But this has been the story of the Singapore Malay/Muslim community contributing to the nation as a Community of Success, always adapting and always quietly finding unique solutions to our own challenges when they arise.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In the 1970s, we established the Mosque Building and Mendaki Fund, tapping on every working Muslim adult to fund and build our mosques so that no foreign money and influence will find its way here.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Recently, we established important institutions such as the Asatizah Recognition Scheme so that only our home-grown religious leaders in our Madrasahs can preach here.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But our quiet peaceful way to resolve our religious challenges internally has been broken.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap earlier asked for nurses and those serving in uniformed services during the Budget to be allowed to wear the tudung.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We emphathise with the views of those who want to don the tudung as part of their uniform in nursing.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is not the first time Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap has raised this, as have other People's Action Party (PAP) Malay/Muslim Members of Parliament previously.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Indeed, many Muslim women contribute meaningfully and serve our nation and society through noble jobs such as nursing and their contributions have been tremendous, especially during the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our Government's secular stand has been consistently clear when it comes to policy-making.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is our approach when dealing even-handedly with requests from different religious groups, especially when it affects our common spaces.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This point was made by Minister K Shanmugam earlier and I note that the Leader of the Opposition, Mr Pritam Singh, agreed to such an approach during MHA's Committee of Supply debate.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In our multi-racial society, in services that play critical roles in our society, the uniform is a visible sign that the service is rendered equally, regardless of race or religion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We do not want patients to prefer or not prefer to be served by a Muslim nurse, nor do we want people to think that public security is being enforced by a Muslim or non-Muslim Police officer.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is what makes the decision difficult and sensitive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Public aggressive pressure on such an issue can only make compromise harder.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Any Government concession to religious pressure will cause other groups to take note and adopt a similar aggressive posture.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is as enjoined by Ms Rahayu Mahzam just now.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We previously engaged unions, religious teachers, and respected members of the community, and they understand why we have adopted our current approach on uniforms in the Public Service.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In this regard, let me again state that I empathise that some Muslim women may find it challenging to choose or remain in professions where they personally find it difficult to fulfil both religious and professional duties at the same time at some point in their life.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, workplaces are an important part of the common space that we share with our fellow Singaporeans and we must not withdraw from them.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As a community, we have been adept at making adaptations and adjustment while at the same time, been able to practice our religion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us take the example of our mosques.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With the help of the Government, we have built mosques in housing estates over the years, right next to homes of fellow Singaporeans of different and various races and religions.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The azan is also played on the Malay radio channel.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As Singaporeans, we understand and respect each other's religious beliefs and practices.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is how we have adjusted as a community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: But it has not limited our faith, but instead, allowed it to thrive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: And new mosques can continue to be built in our heartlands.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We recognise that Mr Faisal Manap may not agree with our Government's approach and continues to open up this topic in public discourse.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Nevertheless, at the heart of our approach is our desire to protect the precious harmony that we have built over the years with other communities in Singapore, and fulfil our religious needs and always consider to do what is best in the interest of our multi-racial and multi-religious nation.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This desire to protect racial and religious harmony is aligned with Islamic teaching.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: What we want is to strengthen our relationships across communities and work towards the common good.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, we must be respectful of the secular nature of our state and maintain our common space even as we look for outcomes that will fulfil the aspirations of our community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I call on our community to reflect how precious this peace and harmony is to us as Muslims.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us not focus on issues that will be divisive.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This issue reminds me of a quote that I would like to share with Members. "The Islamic belief system is built upon pillars of guidance, not compulsion.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Brotherhood and sisterhood, not enmity." Our local asatizah also hold this view, that the religion inculcates these values that spur us to find pragmatic solutions in complex situations.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, I began by sharing how proud I am of how the Malay/Muslim community has adjusted quickly to the COVID-19 pandemic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This would not have been possible without the strong leadership of MUIS working with our asatizah, together with strong support of everyone in the community.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together with leaders of other faith communities, we condemned the attack and affirmed efforts to ensure peaceful and harmonious relations are always maintained among our diverse communities, even in a crisis such as this pandemic.

speaker: The Minister-in-charge of Muslim Affairs (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is how our community demonstrates citizenry, standing united with everyone in Singapore regardless of race or religion.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, let me begin by wishing all the women in the House and all the women in Singapore a very Happy International Women's Day.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This was evident when the pandemic disrupted our daily lives, affected the livelihood of some and strained our economy.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The M³ agencies worked closely with other Malay/Muslim organisations through the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce to support the Malay/Muslim community during this challenging time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This gotong royong spirit is not new to the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is the cornerstone of active citizenry within our community, where we support one another and help uplift the vulnerable and less fortunate, so that we can overcome the crisis and lead meaningful lives.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will continue to strengthen this gotong royong spirit through three key areas.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we will expand our outreach to engage more families, specifically the vulnerable and lower income families and uplift their lives; Second, we will enhance our community engagement capabilities to harness community resources and provide more meaningful support to those in need; and Thirdly, we will strive to empower an engaged community towards greater sense of citizenry in pursuit of our vision of a community of success.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to continue in Malay.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In Malay):   M³@Towns has grown over the last two years, with a suite of programmes rolled out by its agencies.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Abdul Samad asked about measures to fulfil the various needs of the different segments in our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: First, we have programmes to support our young couples in building strong and resilient families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise that there will be negative effects in divorces, especially on the children.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Thus, to help and prepare couples have a good start to their marriage and reduce the likelihood of divorce, we started the "Bersamamu" programme in 2019.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Ms Nadia Ahmad Samdin also asked about the latest progress of this programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As elaborated by Minister Masagos earlier, through this programme, our Naib Kadi have taken the lead to expand and strengthen the support that is provided.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They not only solemnise the marriage, but provide advice and support to couples prior to their marriage and continue providing guidance during the first two years of their marriage.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Second, we also complement the existing efforts in supporting inmates and ex-offenders, as well as their families, through the FITRAH programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Families of inmates with young children will certainly need support if their family member, especially their parents, are incarcerated.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The FITRAH community befrienders help refer affected families to M3 programmes and other Government schemes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We call upon more members of the community who are interested to step forward as a befriender for this programme.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To further expand our reach to the community, we launched two more M³ towns at Geylang Serai and Jalan Besar.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: M³@Toa Payoh will also be launched soon, making it a total of 11 M³@Towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to reach out to more families, especially the vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We do not want anyone to be left behind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, one of M³@Jalan Besar's efforts is reaching out to rental-flat families staying at Jalan Kukoh, to understand their living situation and needs, render assistance and inspire them to better their living standards.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will also raise their awareness about our various programmes and Government schemes, and improve access for them and their children to these programmes, and therefore pave the way for a better life for them.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: COVID-19 has highlighted the need for us to address the digital divide faced by vulnerable families, including our senior citizens.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a community, we must do more to reach out to this group, and assure them that they are not alone in this difficult time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We must ensure that children from these families have access to digital devices to facilitate their learning and development.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: It is therefore timely that we transform the way we reach out to these families to one that is more impactful and caters to their needs.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We want to inspire positive intergenerational mobility, and help their children succeed and secure a brighter future.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We recognise that some may need more support in terms of financial resources.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They also require support in terms of learning tools and in picking up skills.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Some may even face difficulties in accessing our programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Abdul Samad and Mr Sharael Taha highlighted some families may be unaware or are unsure where to go after they have been rejected from our programmes or schemes previously.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: I agree with them that more needs to be done to raise awareness about the support available.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For a start, we will do more to engage and befriend these families, so that we can understand challenges better.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This has been started at M³@Bedok, for instance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Our volunteers have visited over 500 households in Bedok to understand the families better and connect them to the relevant programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One volunteer is Mr Razali Bin Subir, who is also an MAEC grassroots leader in Bedok.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He befriended a senior citizen, 54 years old, who is a caregiver to two young children, one of whom is a special needs child.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: She did not know the platforms to get assistance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: After getting to know her via engagement efforts at M³@Bedok, Mr Razali quickly referred her to MENDAKI and the FITRAH Office, who then connected the family to the mosque to apply for zakat financial assistance.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: They were also referred to their local Family Service Centre to receive counselling support.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
