text: Today, the family is receiving support under the various M³ and national programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Instances like this inspire us to continue improving our work.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We will gradually roll out such engagements across the other M³ towns.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Over the past few months, I have met the M³@Town volunteers, as well as MESRA's volunteers, and I am heartened by their commitment and strong support to be part of this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In addition, M³ will also continue to find ways to partner with other organisations, including Government agencies, to leverage on digital solutions and data to strengthen the effectiveness of our efforts.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Abdul Samad asked about the progress of the SGTeguhBersatu Taskforce that was formed last year.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: By working with other Malay/Muslim organisations, we were able to reach out to various groups more effectively.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, the Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry supported home-based businesses to apply for the Government's Temporary Relief Fund at that time.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through ECO, we want to strengthen such partnerships and work with the MMOs and other community groups to co-create solutions and meet the needs of our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about measures to support volunteers so that they can be more ready and confident in reaching out and supporting vulnerable families.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Through this approach, we hope to build a confident pool of volunteers, who are able to engage families better, and more meaningfully.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, our programmes would not be successful without our volunteers and community partners.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We are fortunate to have attracted a diverse pool of dedicated volunteers who have been supporting our programmes, from planning to execution.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In fact, we are deeply encouraged to have more professionals who also volunteer on the ground with us, while providing and bringing their own expertise and ideas into our programmes.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: For example, a group of lawyers collaborated with MESRA in November last year to organise a free application exercise for Lasting Power of Attorney, or LPA.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This initiative attracted over 300 Malay/Muslim applicants who registered themselves and their loved ones for LPA.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: One lawyer who was part of this initiative is Mr Muslim Albakri, who is 33 years old.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: To Mr Muslim, who runs his own legal practice, giving back to the community is a core tenet to his legal practice.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: He also provides pro-bono legal advice to M³@Town residents as he wants to raise legal awareness and literacy within the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Recently, Mr Muslim and his friends from this group of lawyers launched a website M3lawyers.sg to provide legal assistance to the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The M³@Towns are platforms for professionals to give back to the community in their own ways.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: During the "CiptaSama@M³" sessions in January this year, many also shared their views and vision for the community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Many spoke about the need to promote volunteerism within our community, and to ensure the vulnerable in our community is not left behind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Being part of M³ as a volunteer is one way to contribute.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: In the spirit of Singapore Together, let us be a part of this journey together to develop our community.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Just as the strength of a knot depends on how it is tied together, the strength of a community lies in the unity of its members.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We have created this platform to hear from you, and work together with you.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: We invite you to join us in making impactful changes to those in need.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Together, we can thrive and progress as a Community of Success.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: As a Malay proverb goes, "Just like how water has a circle shape when it flows through a bamboo, the success of our community is achieved when we all work together".

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to conclude in English.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, M³ has grown in strength and we will continue to work hand-in-hand with the various Malay/Muslim organisations and volunteers to ensure that our programmes are effective in meeting the evolving needs of the Malay/Muslim community and ensure no one is left behind.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The community has also made significant progress as a result.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: The gotong royong spirit is one we must encourage – where community members look out for one another and where we empower them to be contributing members of our society.

speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office and Second Minister for Education and Foreign Affairs (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
text: This sense of citizenry will carry us far in navigating uncertainties ahead of us, together with the rest of Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, 2020 has taught us important lessons in adaptability and resilience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I am heartened at how well the M3 platform – MENDAKI, MUIS and MESRA – worked for the Malay/Muslim community and was adapted quickly to help our beneficiaries and the vulnerable.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: I will expand on the three strategies that MENDAKI will be embarking on to take the community forward, to prepare them for the future, and to shape future generations.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, equipping our community, especially our young, with the necessary skills and values to thrive in this digital age and the future economy; second, ensuring our workforce remain relevant to the current economy and prepare them for the future; and third, empowering our youth through mentorship so that they can excel and inspire one another to fulfil their potential while giving back to the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in Malay.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In Malay):   I will expand on the three strategies for MENDAKI to prepare the Malay/Muslim community for a digital economy in the future, and shape future generations that will be more resilient.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: First, we need to ensure that young Malay/Muslims possess the capabilities and skills to thrive in the digital economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: If the foundation is weak, there will be the risk that the child will be left behind in life, compared to other children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, we want parents to play a more prominent role to ensure that their children receive at least three years of pre-school education to prepare them for primary school.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: That is why we introduced KelasMateMatika@CC (KMM@CC) in 2018 – so that parents can be more involved in their children’s early childhood development.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Parents who took part in KMM@CC and its related activities have shared that it has helped them to keep up with the education and digital learning landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: They also received expert advice about good practices in guiding their children.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim asked about the benefits of KMM@CC and MENDAKI's plans to continue to enhance the framework for pre-school education.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Children who have graduated from KMM@CC will be eligible to join KSS.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It will incorporate computational thinking, mathematical concepts, and literacy and writing skills, as will outdoor learning and storytelling.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will help develop the child’s problem-solving skills – and thus enhancing the child’s Primary 1 readiness.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Zhulkarnain also asked about MENDAKI's efforts to ensure continual support to children and youth during Phase 3.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This pandemic has accelerated the adoption of digitalisation, including a shift towards the way we learn and teach.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI also conducted its the MENDAKI Tuition Scheme (MTS) online.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: M³ introduced the eKMM@CC (e-KelasMateMatika@CC) so that parents and children can continue with their lessons online from home.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This mode of learning will continue for the rest of the year, in line with the COVID-19 SMM.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Second, the economy and job landscape are constantly changing.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The Malay/Muslim workforce needs to work hard to continue adapting and stay relevant to the needs of the economy and jobs landscape.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This will help them to prepare for the future and future-proof themselves because the demands for skills or jobs are expected to change to meet the needs of businesses, industries and the economy.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Therefore, we must always adapt and upskill ourselves.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Last October, M3 launched its fourth focus area to improve the employment and employability of our workforce regardless of their age or educational background.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To achieve this objective, MENDAKI SENSE has been working closely with Government agencies such as WSG, SSG, e2i and also Malay/Muslim organisations such as AMP and SMCCI.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These numbers has doubled compared to the previous year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: While COVID-19 has affected employment, there are still jobs and skills opportunities available under the SG United Jobs and Skills Package in sectors such as information and communication, manufacturing and food services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We should be ready with the relevant skills to be able to seize these new opportunities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To answer Mr Abdul Samad’s question, I would like to give the example of 28-year-old Mr Muhammad Farhan.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He is a diploma graduate in Outdoor Adventures Learning who has work experience in customer service.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Unfortunately, due to COVID-19, he was unable to secure a job related to his qualification and had to explore other industries.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: He attended MENDAKI SENSE's career fair and was offered a position as a Wharfside Specialist with BigFoot Logistics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Although this was a new industry for him, he kept an open mind and was able to use his operational and communications skills from his former work experience to his current job.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: With an open mind, we will also be able to explore new opportunities and shape our careers in the long run.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat and Mr Sharael Taha asked about measures to further nurture expertise in the green and digital economy and within the Malay/Muslim community so that our workers, specifically those working in sunset industries, remain relevant.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This includes conducting more digital courses for all seniors through the National Silver Academy (NSA) since Phase 2 commenced.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: The digital courses by SENSE equip our mature workers to seize job opportunities that will now require digital tools and systems.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: It also increases the employability of mature workers in today's economic climate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: This has the potential to benefit mature workers by so that they can acquire relevant skills without worrying about the issue of language.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: MENDAKI's Future Ready Department has also organised several sessions of the "Future of…" Series to various groups of students.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Industries covered include growth industries such as Agri-tech, Engineering and Artificial Intelligence as well as Data Analytics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: These sessions help the youth to gain a better understanding of the ecosystem and skillsets needed within the industry.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: To answer Mr Sharael’s query, MENDAKI is working with STEM partners (Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics) such as Google and Amazon Web Services to offer MTS students opportunities to participate in interest and skills-building programmes such as AWS Educate.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, please allow me to continue in English.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, it is important for our youths to have the right mentors and peer support system that they can turn to for advice while navigating through life.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Sharael asked for an update on the Youth Mentoring Office (YMO) and its future plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: We would like to encourage more within the community to step forward with their expertise and knowledge to play a part in moulding the future of the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about mentoring programmes for high-risk youths.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, it would be more appropriate to have high-risk youths attended to and looked after by professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Based on their profiles and needs, appropriate interventions can be provided by MSF, MOE and social service agencies (SSAs).

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: However, this does not mean that there is no scope for mentoring.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: There is room for mentoring to supplement the professional intervention and certainly, we look forward to the Member's assistance and support for this initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: Mr Chairman, despite the challenges posed by COVID-19, the community has responded well, rallying each other forward during these difficult times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence and Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
text: And I am confident we can face whatever challenges that come our way and emerge stronger as a community of success.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I thought I should address the three clarifications that Mr Faisal Manap had asked at the presentation of his cuts.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MUIS takes a serious view of deviant teachings that can mislead the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MUIS will assess these complaints and together with the Fatwa Committee, will take appropriate measures to deal with these complaints.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These include the inssuance of fatwa counselling and public education.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Where necessary, the Fatwa Committee will issue a fatwa and share relevant information with the public to immediately stop the spread of deviant teachings within the community.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This has been effective in educating the community and preventing the public from falling prey to the false teachings of Islam.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: MUIS takes a holistic and proactive approach in monitoring compliance with the requirements under the MUIS' halal certification framework.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This applies to recognition of foreign bodies certifying food as we need to ensure their credibility and processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: When allegations were raised last year, MUIS responded quickly to investigate into the matter in a very rigorous and thorough manner.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Some critics may have said that the investigation process took too long.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But the same critics also called on MUIS to interview even more stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Having reviewed the report, I can assure Members that the investigation process was robust and deliberate with opportunity provided to all interested parties to put submissions to MUIS to be reviewed.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Interviews were also conducted as deemed necessary to gather further evidence, which has also written to the delisted Foreign Halal Certifying Bodies (FHCBs) to furnish details on the reasonable objective grounds that led to their delistment.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We want a proper closure so that there are no other doubts raised after this.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the JAKIM issue, the Member of Parliament Faisal Manap raised the issue of this alleged meat cartel in Malaysia which was based on media reports – all from Malaysia though.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Non-halal meat was being imported to Malaysia and certified halal.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is a separate issue for an investigation and we have stated this in our media statement, which was issued together with MUIS and Singapore Food Agency (SFA).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So I hope our Member does not just read the Malaysian version.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Based on the Malaysian media report, the meat cartel issue in Malaysia is being investigated by authorities, and then, some actions have been taken with individuals involved.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the quote mentioned by the JAKIM officer that such mislabelling is happening in Singapore, MUIS is unaware of the background of his statement.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On Irsyad, Member of Parliament Faisal Manap also raised the issues of governance of Madrasah Irsyad.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This is the kind of issue to be put up in the open; if there are doubts, responded to, and if there are issues that has to be dealt with the law, we will deal with it to the end.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the Member of Parliament has not sent the queries ahead of time, I am not able to provide a full response at this time to the various queries.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, I invite him to file a Parliamentary Question (PQ) on the matter so that we can address this fully.

speaker: The Chairman
text: We have about 10 minutes before we move on to the next cut.

speaker: The Chairman
text: So, we can take clarifications arising out of the cuts discussed now before we move on with the debate.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: Chairman, I have two clarifications for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: First, my question on the deviant teaching, I would just like the Minister to clarify, and if I can repeat my question in Malay.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: (In Malay):   When was the first complaint received by MUIS about this individual who practice deviant teaching?

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: (In English): On the issue of discussion on tudung, Sir, I would like to offer myself to the Minister to be part of this closed door discussion.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I am not privy to any of the discussions being done, behind closed doors.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I believe that as the Minister had mentioned, it only involves PAP Malay Members of Parliament.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I feel all elected Malay Members of Parliament should be part of this closed door discussion.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, maybe through my involvement as well as the involvement of other elected Malay Members of Parliament in the discussion behind closed doors, I may consider not to bring or to surface what is deemed by Minister Masagos as insensitive and divisive issues.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I do want a response from the Minister on this whether all the Malay elected Members of Parliament can be part of this discussion as well as other discussions which involve the relevant Malay agencies such as MENDAKI, MUIS, maybe not MAC but MENDAKI and MUIS?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There was a similar Parliamentary Question filed on the deviant teaching, a recent one.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope the Member can refer to that because we did put the dates and what we were doing in that particular case.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, it was not that I have never done it with the Member.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Minister Maliki, are you wanting to take the rostrum?

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This issue relates to Mr Faisal Manap's earlier comment, both during his speech in the Budget debate as well as the current discussion we are having on allowing nurses and those in uniform services to wear tudung.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I echo first Minister Masagos' views that we do empathise with the views of those who want to don the tudung as part of their uniform in nursing.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They agree that these are sensitive issues and best discussed behind closed doors.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: They also agree that the solution is not straightforward and we should not rush into one without addressing these other concerns.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And whether Mr Faisal Manap participates in these sessions or not, I think the most important thing is a large segment of the community has been consulted and we continue to consult them.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Uniforms serve to project the common identity which in turn develops esprit de corps and strengthen camaraderie.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In the case of public healthcare services, the uniform underscores that our healthcare workers are neutral and provide impartial care regardless of race and religion.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is a reminder on both the healthcare workers as well as the persons receiving the care.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: This is in addition to the uniform meeting operational and safety requirements.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We can attest to this through our own personal experiences.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: I was just hospitalised a few months back and I can attest to them performing their duties with the utmost respect from all of us.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But even so, and even more importantly, they perform it during national crises like SARS and more currently, COVID-19, par excellence.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: There are Muslim scholars, Sir, who have given guidance that Muslims must make appropriate adjustments while staying true to their faith when living in a plural and contemporary society.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We must avoid situations like in other countries, where issues of religious expression take centre stage, become a divisive matter and put certain groups under the spotlight.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The Grand Imam of al-Azhar, His Excellency Dr Ahmed Al-Tayeb came to Singapore.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: He spoke about the tudung when he delivered the MUIS Lecture in Singapore in 2018.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: So, on issues that affect our common space, we must always approach them very carefully.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap may not agree with our approach, but this is our approach.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Our religious scholars and community leaders support our approach as they understand that these issues, especially those that involve racial and religious sensitivities, are complex and any decision on them should not be taken lightly.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We must also ensure that our approach in addressing such issues safeguards the harmony between all races and religions in Singapore.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As articulated earlier, Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap had on previous occasions also raised this issue and he had articulated before that he is doing so because it is his job as a Member of Parliament to give feedback to the Government.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We must know that our role as Members of Parliament is more than just giving feedback and reflecting public sentiment in the open, even in the Parliament.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Yes, there is nothing that we cannot bring up in the Parliament.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But PAP Muslim Members of Parliament also recognise our role as leaders of our communities.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: As leaders, we must exercise discretion and know the implications of our actions.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We are leaders and we have the responsibility to ensure our collective desired outcome as a society and country to maintain racial and religious harmony.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Thus, as leaders, we have to lead our community to understand sensitivities – when they cannot initially, maybe – of such topics and issues which are best not discussed in the open.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: If you are not careful, any discussion in the open may lead to serious ramifications.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: Mr Chairman and colleagues, I must tell you it is not easy.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: But we must do and we need to do what is right.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We do our best to convince our community leaders, our religious leaders and our union leaders.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: We hope that they will also, in their own ways, discuss these matters with their members constructively, yet in private, away from the glare of the public.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: And I hope Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap can do likewise.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: If he wants to speak to community leaders, he can do so, but do so away from the glare of the public and that is what we should remember.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: In fact, just a few weeks ago, I spoke to a group of union leaders and we spoke about these issues in private.

speaker: Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman
text: The community leaders understand these sensitivities when it comes to race and religion.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I have a few sets of clarifications to ask.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: One, perhaps addressed to Senior Minister of State Zaqy Mohamad, I am quite excited by the announcement of Kelas Siap Sekolah (KSS), the pilot by MENDAKI.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Perhaps the Senior Minister of State can share a bit more on what the age range and what are the minute details for this KSS programme.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I filed a few Parliamentary Questions on the halal certification and I am quite heartened by the response by the Minister on 1 February that MUIS is engaging all stakeholders and foreign halal certification bodies (FHCBs), and that the details for the review will be announced later this year.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I would just like to ask whether there is any progress and whether considerations can be made to the implementation of the ASEAN Cooperation Action Plan on Halal Food and the establishment of the international Halal authority body during the course of this review.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As my colleague Mr Zaqy Mohamad is making his way to the podium, if you do not mind, Mr Chairman, I will take the second question first.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We would like to have a cooperating framework for the halal system because this will facilitate the movement of halal goods and so forth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But in Singapore, we also work within the many other laws and regulations to ensure not just the "halal-ness" of our food but also hygiene and pricing issues that will be faced by our consumers and so forth.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, we will work also first to address our interest for our community as well as for Singapore; and then look at how the others can then fall in together with us to make sure that we have a consistent, a cogent halal framework for even ASEAN.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But as I mentioned, once I say I am going to look at what I need for Singapore, I am quite sure the other countries will do the same.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, this journey to get to where we want to be will probably be some generalisation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The specific way to address this issue will take some time to come.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I will keep it short, bearing in mind time constraints.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this will involve our kids from four to six; and hopefully, help them to adapt to Primary school better.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the MENDAKI-MUIS Preschool Grant (MMPG), I will just do an update.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Of these 80 children, 67 of them had their parents' savings in the Child Development Account (CDA) and 64% of them have achieved an attendance of at least 70% at their pre-schools.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: We will continue to give them maximum support, working together with ECDA and MSF, because we want to encourage parents to send their kids for pre-school education so that they are better prepared for Primary school.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I will take two more clarifications, but please keep them short.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Wan Rizal and then, I will circle back to Mr Muhamad Faisal Abdul Manap.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Indeed, these are sensitive issues that should be handled with much care.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: I am also grateful to note that these conversations are on-going and have been made with various segments of the community.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Earlier, the Ministers mentioned about the importance of asatizah within the community and I am in agreement with their dedication, their ability and of course, their influence.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask on the role of our asatizah in this regard.

speaker: Dr Wan Rizal (Jalan Besar)
text: How can they continue to work with the Government on handling such sensitive issues so that the community is also convinced that the religious sector can provide them with the right and appropriate guidance?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This, indeed, is one of the difficult areas that MUIS has for the longest time since its formation, uniting our community, uniting asatizah, so that not only will they fulfil their duties and obligations as religious teachers but also understand how that can be done and even when it ought to be done.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, this continued engagement that we have with them, whether through their regulatory bodies like the Asatizah Recognition Board (ARB) or through the associations like Pergas, must be on-going.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If there are new developments, we will update them and think about how we can move forward.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I think the real question the Member is asking is when will this happen?

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If you have already agreed with someone you are going to marry, you can have a wedding date.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But when you are dating, I do not think you have a wedding date or time to decide with your partner, "We better decide this by this time or else we go together or not together".

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, when we resolve matters like this, we cannot resolve it with a deadline.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Instead, it is one where we engage and prepare the ground; continue to engage and prepare the ground.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, that when the moment comes and we have to make a decision, it brings the least impact to those affected.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And hopefully, even, because we have done this groundwork, address their issues and hopefully, they accept it with the generosity and the goodwill that we have as fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But that is what you get when you invest time to build relationship, trust with each other.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I hope that we can get to the answer, when we can do this, as soon as we find the solutions and the considerations being addressed.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap, please keep your clarification tight.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I appreciate him sharing that indeed we had a closed door person-to-person talk on this issue last year.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: So, I like to just to ask the Minister whether you can extend the trust that you have in me in discussing such things behind closed doors, in a really formal closed-door setting.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I just like to hear from the Minister.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: He did mention that there are some countries where tudungs are not being allowed to be donned by nurses because it causes divisiveness.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: But in contrast, I kind of recall there are quite a number of countries like Australia, New Zealand and the UK, actually, that allow the tudung to be donned.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: I would like Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman to at least share a country or two which he was referring to earlier.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: By speaking to the Member personally, I am involving him and I am treating him specially.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Because I want this to be a heart-to-heart talk with him and exchange our views, and not open ourselves to speaking in a setting which we may have to constrain or hold ourselves.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I will continue with the Member if he wants to.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We can talk and we will continue to talk.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But I urge the Member to continue to look at the situation in a very special way because this is about racial harmony, religious harmony and the peace that we have with each other.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Do not disturb it by putting up a sensitive topic like this that may spur some part of our community to actions that we may regret later on.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: On the issue of why other countries can do it, there are many things that other countries do that we do not do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We are Singaporeans, we do what is good by Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: If you want to do something that they like, we must also then, do what we do not like that they do.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I do not think we want that either.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We do what is good for us, our community, our nation.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: And I hope as Members of Parliament, we swore to uphold and preserve our Constitution; let us do that.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think the Minister has replied to both your clarifications.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I do not think there is a need for Dr Maliki to take the rostrum?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Chairman, I will speak on the role of People's Association (PA).

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I share the sentiments expressed by the hon Member Sylvia Lim as far back as the 2016 COS debate regarding PA’s huge budget and unclear mandate.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Despite the queries of many non-PAP Members subsequent to that, many questions remain unanswered.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: First, the question of why the PA is allocated such a huge budget.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, PA’s cost per staff is even higher than that of IRAS and GovTech, which are supposed to have a higher proportion of professional staff.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Why is such an expensive administration structure needed when the main job of PA is to be a bridge between the Government and the citizens, and much of the work of the PA is carried out by the grassroot volunteers and volunteer worker organisations (VWOs)?

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We wholeheartedly support the hard work put up by the staff and volunteers of PA to strengthen the social fabric of our country.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If it is so heavily funded by taxpayers’ money, we wish that the PA is a real organisation for the people with its leadership and membership not skewed towards any political party.

speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In view of the recent debate on the CDCs, we would also like to know the CDC's budget as a percentage of the PA's budget.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Ms Joan Pereira, if you would like to take both your cuts together, please do.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Chairman, the disruption to our economy from the pandemic has had different impact on various segments of our country.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: COVID-19 has inflicted disproportionate hardship upon those who are less well-off and pushed those at the margins into further difficulties.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: To make matters worse, rampant misinformation on the internet and social media platforms is adding to the turbulence.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Our world is under many stresses and these have the potential to deepen societal divisions, especially those along religious and racial fault lines.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There is much work to be done to narrow the gaps.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We need to foster a cohesive and caring society in order to recover and forge ahead as one nation.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MCCY share its strategies on how it will work with Singaporeans to close ranks and become a more united and resilient people?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: How will the Government ensure that in our fight against the pandemic and consequent chaos, no one is left behind?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of my greatest concerns is the state of racial and religious harmony in Singapore.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It is threatened by radicalisation of troubled individuals and groups.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Strengthening religious harmony is an on-going work in progress.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: We are one of the most religiously diverse countries in the world.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Mutual respect and tolerance are qualities that we must all conscientiously nurture and practice, and teach our young.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Similarly, we need to put in effort to encourage Singaporeans to do their part to build racial harmony.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: The more we interact with members of different racial communities, the better we can understand one another and learn that in fact, we have so much more in common than differences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: What is exciting for me is that there is much wisdom we can gather from those who are different from us.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Would MCCY share the projects and initiatives it has in store to further enhance our racial harmony?

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: One of the silver linings from the COVID-19 pandemic is how it ignited the spirit of “gotong royong” in our society.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: There are various interpretations and translations for this phrase, including “active citizenry”, “cooperation in a community” and “mutual aid”.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: My favorite is “carrying burdens together” because gotong means "carrying a burden using one's shoulder" and royong means "together" or "communally".

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Carrying burdens together implies a willingness to help another lighten his load.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: It means stepping forward to volunteer and lend a helping hand.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: During this crisis, many individuals, businesses and community groups have indeed stepped up.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: They voluntarily contributed time, energy and money to organise their own ground-up initiatives to assist those in need.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: This outpouring of selflessness brought strangers and the community together in a common cause.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I am heartened and inspired by the efforts of our people to work together for the benefit of our community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I earnestly hope that we will be able to continue the momentum and sustain this spirit of mutual care, trust and understanding.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Even as we are helping the needy, we are simultaneously building bonds across religious, racial and cultural boundaries, and learning more about ourselves and our Singapore identity.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: A student volunteer shared how he would never look at a packet of food the same way again after helping to distribute packets of meals to some needy families.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Coming from a very comfortable background, it was hard for him to visualise food insecurity in our bustling city.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: His experience as a volunteer had been an eye opener and strengthened his resolve to be more involved in the community.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Each one of us has a different takeaway from our volunteering experiences.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Such sharing and interactive sessions will be helpful for bonding and motivating one another to stay involved and keep going.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Otherwise, some of them may feel alone along the volunteering journey and drop off.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: On the other hand, if they enjoy the volunteering journey, they will encourage their family members, friends and relatives to join them.

speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Sharing is also helpful if boredom or inertia sets in as fellow volunteers can give advice about different ways of contributing or even make a change to another cause.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: To make things worse, we witnessed insensitive misinformation propagated on media platforms threatening to strain our societal fault lines and heighten the tension that the pandemic already caused us.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: However, I am heartened that my fellow Singaporeans have risen to the occasion.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Singaporeans rallied around one another to keep each other safe.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We have read and seen heart-warming acts of ordinary Singaporeans giving out free masks, placing hand sanitisers in lifts, neighbours helping one another to deliver groceries, free food in appreciation of healthcare workers and more.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Donation collections also increased for some charities, despite the challenging circumstances.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: These self-initiated acts of kindness demonstrate the good in our people and reflect the strong foundation of our social values.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Contrast these with the irrational acts of violence targeting Asian communities in the West; ranging from assaulting elderly Asians on the streets, vandalising businesses operated by Asians to calling for Asians to be deported.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: We cannot let any form of prejudice and discrimination poison our society.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Our diverse and harmonious society today is hard earned and too precious to lose.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: On this note, I would like to ask two questions.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: First, what are the Government’s strategies in strengthening Singapore’s cohesion and resilience so that all Singaporeans can forge ahead together as one?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Second, how will the Ministry strengthen its effort in bridging the different segments of our diverse society?

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: To quote Mother Theresa, “I can do things you cannot, you can do things I cannot; together we can do great things”.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui, if you would like to take your two cuts together, please do.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Chairman, since the circuit breaker, Singapore and Singaporeans underwent a dramatic transformation, quickly learning to adjust to the new normal of working and playing from home.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Whilst social distancing and the strict no mixing rules are essential, there is a downside.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: If you limit social interactions in person, we will seek it online.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: We form chat groups and the online space quickly becomes an echo chamber.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Our preciously woven social fabric will start to fray.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: If he had more exposure to Muslims teens through social interactions, would things have been different?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Another case, in February 2021, a 16-year-old Indian boy was missing and last seen in the Bukit Batok vicinity.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The SPF appealed for public help to spot the missing teen.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: All these can be found online, in public.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: These two prominent cases happening cannot be isolated incidents.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: These are the initial clarion calls of a deeper, more troubling reality.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Is this the outcome of people flocking online?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: This is especially worrying for the youth, due to the higher internet penetration rate and the availability of radical and extreme literature online.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: We must rethink our approach to how we can systematically encourage people of different walks to engage with each other.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: I heard good reviews about Racial Harmony Day in schools but what about schools that do not have a representative number of races?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Perhaps between missionary schools and madrasahs or other culturally oriented schools.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: How many friends from other races do we count among our contacts?

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: This social mixing can start from our school days.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: We should start to re-introduce inter school programmes and activities, allow our rich diversity to be the strength in our social bonds.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: The IRCC should also play a bigger role.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: In the past, it was easier to integrate new citizens and PRs as they interact with the community.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui (Tampines)
text: Now, with social media and chatgroups, they tend to form their own chats within their circles.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to declare that I am on the Boards of SISTIC and Esplanade.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Artists, musicians and their work give meaning to the complex world in which we live.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: During the lockdown, Italian tenor Andrea Bocelli performed at an empty Milan Cathedral and lifted the spirits of millions around the world.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Museums offered free virtual tours to all who needed a culture fix while self-isolating.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And I joined Singaporeans all across the island to belt out in solidarity from our balconies, Dick Lee’s “Home Truly”.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Indeed, like Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong said in a speech, “Human beings need the arts and culture to nourish our souls”.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Creative people are, however, resilient people, and the “show must go on".

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Many have pivoted to teaching, and of course, going digital is inevitable.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: SISTIC, for example, had to pivot quickly so as to support our Arts groups and venues to go online.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Esplanade and the Singapore Symphony Orchestra (SSO) were amongst the first to pilot with ticketed livestream performances here, and viewers, including global audiences, were delighted to consume Singapore arts content during the circuit breaker.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: A young Singaporean woman composer/musician, NyaLi shared with me her gratitude for the “Geylang Serai Arts Platform” which helped her to go digital.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I was encouraged to hear NyaLi tell me that she signed up for a course on Digital Marketing and is also using her talents to help the disadvantaged.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: COVID-19 is the burning platform that drives businesses and professionals across all sectors to digitalise, to reskill and to transform; and the Arts is no exception.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Does MCCY plan to scale platforms like Geylang Serai?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Will MCCY support with more shared space for ideation and experimentation?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Is it in MCCY’s plans to bring the creative and tech talents together to co-create new innovative models for the Arts?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: It does not look like large scale events and lounge performances will return in the near future.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And can the social and wellness industries tap on our creative talents?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: I hope that Singaporeans, corporates, the Government and the creative community themselves can come together to strengthen and grow our Singapore creative capital.

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: Now that we even have a University of the Arts, what would have to be true for our creative capital to turn to gold for Singapore, like what K-pop and K-drama did for Korea?

speaker: Ms Janet Ang (Nominated Member)
text: And on that note, let me close with the lyrics from one of NyaLi’s COVID-19 singles: “The world is big and we are small; geography can be so cruel; but I’d like to think that love stands up; tall and proud on her own.” Thank you and I wish everyone Happy International Women’s Day!

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Chairman, COVID-19 has impacted the art sector profoundly.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Many organisations and artists saw their income plummet due to the restrictions around live performances.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Arts practitioners have felt the brunt of the pandemic and many have turned to other sources of income.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Today, I shall touch on the uncertainty felt in the industry, about whether it can emerge stronger through COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Related to earning income, there is also been feedback that the restrictions on live performances appear relatively harsh when compared to other activities.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: For instance, restaurants have customers at the same table at close proximity, chatting and laughing for hours without masks on.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Restaurants can also move their tables or chairs around to maximise their capacity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: In contrast, theatres and concert halls have fixed seats.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: When social distancing measures are applied, some are down to 25% capacity.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: But the audiences are required to sit silently, with masks on during the entire performance.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Venues like the Substation have long been associated with the pursuit of Art for its own sake, understanding that incubation takes time and artists need autonomy and flexibility.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Having spaces managed by independent arts groups gives artists the comfort that those in charge understand the nature of art-making and will accommodate creative spirits as they undertake pioneering endeavours.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: I note that there has been some unease recently about several arts organisations losing their venues for various reasons or being asked to relinquish autonomy over buildings they have long managed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Some of these buildings will be upgraded by the National Arts Council (NAC) and thereafter, be leased by the NAC to multiple users as part of a national plan.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: There have been concerns raised about how such a move would undermine independence in arts creation.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Key concerns cited were the uncertainty of lease renewals, costs and bureaucracy.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
text: Some practitioners have also expressed dissatisfaction with the perceived lack of proper communication about physical spaces before momentous announcements are made.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Chairman, the arts and culture and sports sectors have been severly disrupted by COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: The recent Singapore Tennis Open is a big step forward in our safe, gradual resumption of events and activities, but we far from out of the woods.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Arts and culture and sports are key to our social fabric.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Without these, we would be a poorer society.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Well, actually, without arts and culture and sports, we would be a poor society, full-stop!

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So, arts and culture and sports are essential.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: They are essential to who we are as a society and COVID-19 has made this more salient, not less.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Last year, I served in the Community Care Facility (CCF) for migrant workers who were confirmed COVID-19-positive.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: These workers were taken away from work, away from their dorms, away from their community and had to be in the CCFs until they recover.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: So, anxiety was high – about the disease, about jobs, about their families back home.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Recognising this, a ground-up group partnered us to run art therapy sessions for the workers in the CCF.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Not only that, it made a real impact.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: The act of creating art was a cathartic outlet for the workers, and so we ran as many sessions as we could; facilitators, translators, all in full PPEs.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: This, I think, is a simple but powerful example of how the arts can uplift all of us in our darkest hour.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: As importantly, what are the plans to help athletes adjust to safety measures and reach peak condition at the right time?

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: In 2018, the Safe Sports Commission was launched, with a mandate to guard against misconduct and abuse in the sports fraternity.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: There are many cautionary tales around the world.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Larry Nassar, who was US gymnastics doctor, assaulted more than 100 female athletes over three decades, including gold medalists McKayla Maroney, Aly Raisman and Gabby Douglas.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: US gymnastics chief Steve Penny resigned too, on accusations of failing to act and quickly notify authorities on the abuse allegations.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: In US swimming on the other hand, more than a hundred coaches have been banned for life for working at affiliated clubs because of abuse allegations as well.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: But the Sports Federation had also been accused of failing to respond adequately to complaints, with some coaches allowed to evade accusers and authorities, moved to new cities and gained coaching jobs at new clubs where they found fresh victims.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: We have done well in Singapore but we cannot take for granted that abuse would not happen here.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: We need to put in place comprehensive measures to ensure sports here remain safe for everyone – men and women, boys and girls, professional, school and community athletes.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: To this end, what else is MCCY doing to ensure safe sports in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay (Nominated Member)
text: Chairman, please allow me to take the next two cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: At the outset, I should declare that I am Chairman of SNOC’s Athletes’ Commission.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: My first cut relates to the safety of travelling national athletes.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In my Budget debate speech, I said that Sports inspires and unites.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Our Team Singapore athletes will have multiple opportunities to fly our flag high at the Olympics, Paralympics and Southeast Asian Games.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I hope that our athletes and support teams harness the opportunity whilst protecting themselves as they train and prepare for their competitions.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I want to thank MCCY and SportSG for making the COVID-19 vaccination available for athletes who need to go abroad for training and competitions.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Although we have these target competitions in mind, the road to these major competitions is long.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: An ambitious plan to have our football team qualify for the World Cup.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: At first glance, it may seem as though it is an impossible task.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: But accomplishing seemingly impossible tasks is something Singapore has no lack of experience in.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Goal 2034 should not focus on the singular achievement of just football and our nation’s endeavour of qualifying for the World Cup.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Success should take a broader perspective covering the other active sports, development systems, culture and the industry.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Goal 2034 presents an excellent opportunity to test our sports ecosystem and be the catalyst that levels up Singapore as a sporting nation.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Many vital factors are critical to the achievement of this goal.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: One, develop a broad base to identify talent.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I believe Singapore has athletic, coaching and administrative talent.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: We have seen Singaporeans achieve on the global stage.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: However, much of this is left to chance.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I hope MCCY can consider how systems can be put in place to identify and groom athletes, coaches and administrators.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I want to ask if our systems and progression pathways are robust and competitive enough to reach Goal 2034.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Are the leagues and divisions competitive enough to groom talent to be world beaters?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Can we definitively say that our leagues are as competitive as the EPL, La Liga, Bundesliga, or Serie A?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: If not, can we enable more Singaporeans to venture overseas and play in more competitive leagues?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In sports that have consistently performed for Singapore, such as swimming, Joseph Schooling and Quah Zheng Wen live and train abroad to spar with the world’s best on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Though most of our national swim team train at the NTC at the Sports Hub’s Aquatic Centre, it took years for the swimming eco-system to develop.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: There is no doubt in my mind that more sports in Singapore need to establish systems and pathways to identify, develop and retain more talent.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Three, create an environment for sports to thrive.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: This entails: (a) enabling Singaporeans to participate and compete in sports safely.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: And I would like to acknowledge hon Members Sitoh Yih Pin and Xie Yao Quan for their comments on the importance of SafeSport; (b) ensure coaches and trainers are given adequate and relevant training that meets the needs of the industry and (c) that there is a vibrant sports industry for businesses to thrive.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: We should continue to enhance the capabilities of SEPs and promote the SMEs in this sector.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is a beloved icon; a familiar friend.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Anyone of us who has taken a long trip abroad – in those days when we could still travel, of course! – and returned will remember the intense longing for that hearty meal of roti prata, satay or char kway teow; and sometimes we would all have them at the same time!

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In this regard, who does not appreciate our Singaporean hawker fare in hawker centres that echo with its trademark chatter of voices, clatter of plates and cups and the warm echoes of friends and family?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must pay tribute to the hawkers, the thousands of men and women who laboured long hours over hot stoves and produced meals to feed Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Not only have they fed our food culture, they have also contributed richly to Singapore’s multiculturalism.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Their meals are economical and highly affordable; and hence, hawker centres are inclusive.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We must therefore preserve our hawker centres so that the award is not more than a trophy to be dusted occasionally.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We need to do so, so that the generations after us will learn and know how this culture evolved.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: If education is the soul of a society, then let us teach our children the origins and vibrant history of our hawker culture: how we evolved from street peddling to the setting up of licensed hawker establishments as a long part of the journey to preserve food safety and hygiene without losing authenticity.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Using digital means and heartwarming stories, our humble hawker history can thus come alive.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We should celebrate our hawker culture as part of the school studies curriculum.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can record, digitally publish, teach and share the recipes and food preparation methods through applications so that our children know the ingredients that make up these unique dishes and discover more about their cultural significance.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chair, there are plenty of nuggets to be unearthed.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For instance, char kway teow is a wok-fried noodle dish has its roots in Teochew culture, originating from the region of Chaozhou, in China’s Guangdong province.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In Cantonese stir-fried cuisine, the reference to “wok hei” literally, "the breath of the wok", is a culinary term used to refer to the harmony of taste in a stir-fried dish.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Even in the 1950s, hawkers learnt to cook char kway teow over firewood rather than gas stoves to retain that smoky "wok hei" aroma.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: And while the ubiquitous roti prata is typically associated with Tamil-speaking Indian-Muslim stalls, the dish apparently has its roots in Northern India, which has a stronger wheat-based culinary culture.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There are many more such nuggets of information.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can also explore new ways to run hawker centres.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would be good to thus see how hawker centres managed by social enterprises – Social Enterprise Hawker Centre (SEHC) – work.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: At SEHCs, hawkers are usually new, unlike those at the legacy hawker centres where hawkers have been selling food for decades.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It would be fitting to glean key management takeaways from both types of hawker centres to encourage the spirit of innovation and keep the heritage of our hawker culture going.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: One could also consider a permanent exhibition at one of our museums to inspire our children and our people through stories of the evolution of the hawker culture.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Or why not even have a permanent “Singapore Hawker Museum”, that would highlight the culinary culture of the dishes while also perhaps tracing the development of hawkers in Singapore, from the street-peddlers to the 21st century hawker centres of today?

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Chair, our hawker centres are our nation’s community kitchens.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Hawker culture is part of our national heritage and I hope that the Government will continue to come up with innovative and creative ways to keep this culture alive.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: The COVID-19 pandemic has inspired a strong kampung spirit and a push towards active citizenry in our society.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: We have witnessed individuals, businesses, and the community step up, came together to organise ground-up initiatives to assist those in need.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Just like in Woodgrove, where residents grassroots volunteers and our community partners, such as schools, VWOs as well as Northwest CDC, came together and lived up to the spirit of ‘From the Community, For the Community’ by organising care pack distribution drives for the vulnerable groups as well as food delivery riders within our community.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: What are the Ministry’s plans to encourage more individuals, such as our youths, our corporations to step forward to work closely with the relevant agencies and other community partners to contribute and leave a positive impact to our community?

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I will address some of the cuts here and my colleagues from the Ministry will take the others.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We can achieve this, through the collective action of everyone.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: United, cohesive, resilient; forging forward together, as Ms Joan Pereira has suggested.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: She and Ms Tin Pei Ling asked about MCCY’s strategies to ensure that our society comes together in the face of uncertainty.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Where we go from here, the paths we choose to take – will define us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And our values and our character will shine through in the choices we make.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And I am moved by how our communities stepped forward and supported one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Tin shared some anecdotal stories, and I am sure many of us in this House will have our own stories.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our community leaders have rallied behind our national vaccination programmes, with senior religious leaders supporting the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All hands on deck, partnering one another and with the Government to build a better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It took stock of about 17,000 reflections and aspirations for us to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But they must also lead to action, and tangible outcomes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, we therefore initiated the Singapore Together Alliances for Action (AfAs).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The AfAs are action-oriented, cross-sector collaborations, tackling complex issues which confront our society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes economic growth opportunities, youth mental well-being, which is a growing important issue, and lower wage workers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The first will be on emerging needs and volunteerism.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will focus on supporting mental wellness, helping seniors adapt to the new normal, and facilitating in-kind contributions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This partners corporates to develop a national framework on corporate purpose and measuring impact, to guide them in doing well by doing good.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Alvin will share more details of these Alliances.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At MCCY, our scope is wide – arts, heritage, youth, sports, community relations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
