text: But at its core, it is about nurturing a more caring people, a more cohesive society and a more confident nation, and building ties that bind us not only to one another, but to the place that we call home, giving us a sense of place and of purpose, anchored to Singapore.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I talked about our Singapore Tapestry last year.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to weave our diverse threads together, and ensure that this Tapestry stays strong and cohesive.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Joan Pereira and Miss Cheng Li Hui asked about our efforts to foster greater social cohesion and mixing among youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY provides opportunities for Singaporeans of diverse backgrounds to interact.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we encourage students to meet through arts and sports.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The National Arts Council and SportSG have been partnering MOE on the Strategic Partnership Co-Curricular Activity (SP-CCA), the pilot that we have initiated in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through this, students not only participate in CCAs based outside of their schools, but they also get a chance to do so with students from other schools, mixing with students from different backgrounds, coming from a diverse range of schools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will be reviewing this pilot to expand the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: SportSG’s Academies and Clubs have programmes for youths across 17 sports, where students can take part in these sports, play with their peers from different schools.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have grown it to 90,000 in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we regularly engage our youths through volunteering activities and leadership development programmes organised by the National Youth Council (NYC), where students practise teamwork and collaboration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we build mutual understanding through shared experiences.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NAC’s WeCare Arts Fund and NHB’s HeritageCares support Social Service Agencies to help beneficiaries access arts and heritage programmes alongside their fellow Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our artists and athletes have played a key role in helping us progress as a cohesive society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our plans to sustain interest in sports, arts and culture and how MCCY will help artists and athletes embrace the new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I think several other Members raised the point as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Ms Janet Ang spoke about how critical the arts is.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As we mature and develop as a society, our arts, our culture, our heritage will only become more essential and a greater and more integral part of us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They not only uplift our spirits but also give expression to our shared heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They help enhance our sense of belonging, binding us together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must continue to develop the sector, by nurturing our artistic talents, providing them with opportunities, spaces and resources to incubate, to experiment, to innovate and to collaborate with one another.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will facilitate creative art-making and presentation, while ensuring that this also benefits the wider arts community, and all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We invested significantly in growing capabilities and audiences through the 2012 Arts and Culture Strategic Review, and Our SG Arts and Heritage Plans launched in 2018.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We also supported arts organisations to deliver a vibrant arts calendar of over 9,000 activities in 2019.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That year, we saw a record high attendance of 15.6 million at arts and culture events, and a record high visitorship of 9.6 million to museums and heritage institutions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, the pandemic has had a profound impact on the sector, a sector that thrives on presence, not only onstage, but in the audience.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Ms Janet Ang talked about the survival of our arts groups, and asked about our plans to support our artists.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: While live performances resumed safely in Phase Three, the return of capacity audiences will take some time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This has to be balanced against the need to keep Singapore and Singaporeans safe.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This, however, has put pressure on arts organisations and artists to cover operating costs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will, therefore, do what we can to safeguard livelihoods and retain capabilities in these sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we will extend the ACRP operating grant and venue hire subsidy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will help our arts organisations and artists defray operating costs, which are usually a substantial portion of the costs that they have to meet each month.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we will introduce new measures to address some specific concerns.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last December, NAC organised two ESCs involving arts organisations and self-employed practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will enhance support for SEPs and gig workers, as Ms Janet Ang had asked, across the sector to collaborate on projects with one another, or, indeed, with other arts organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will help to build capabilities and create more work opportunities for SEPs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It helps us to uplift the arts eco-system, allows there to be a bit of a mix-and-match kind of approach, and this grant is aimed at preserving that.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Whilst we focus on these matters, we also must have a clear eye on what a post-pandemic arts eco-system must look like.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: To this end, we have introduced a new Business Transformation Fund.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will support the transformation of arts and culture organisations, as well as support their recovery and sustainability in a post-pandemic situation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to do this collaboratively because we are stepping into a new normal, one that may last for some time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, NAC will engage stakeholders to gather views on these new schemes, so that we can refine them where necessary before they are launched in a few months, in June 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, we will continue to help the sector build capabilities that will see them through in the longer term.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NAC will continue to provide training grants to our cultural practitioners.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include on-going schemes like the Capability Development Grant which have supported artists since 2012.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY also supports MOE’s initiative to form an alliance between LASALLE and NAFA.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The new arts University will further develop the creative capacity of our youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It facilitates learning and networking opportunities across creative disciplines and provides industry-relevant training.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We established the Cultural Matching Fund (CMF) in 2013, to provide a dollar-for-dollar matching of private cash donations to arts and heritage charities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This growth in cultural philanthropy has been sustained with the top-up of CMF in 2017 and we wish to keep up this spirit of giving.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, this is the one fund that when I sit down and discuss the Budget with the Deputy Prime Minister, I did not mind telling him it was depleted – because it tells us that we have built up an active culture of arts patronage and philanthropy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And we will review the CMF with MOF, with a view towards an additional top-up of the fund in 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Minister of State Low Yen Ling will speak more about MCCY’s plans to support our arts and heritage sectors to innovate and also deliver programmes in this new normal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2012, SportSG launched Vision 2030 as a roadmap to empower Singaporeans to Live Better Through Sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was reviewed in 2019, leading to the launch of Vision 2030 Recharged! where we renewed focus on tailoring programmes for various segments of the population.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over the years, we have built new sports centres under the Sports Facilities Master Plan and also rejuvenated existing ones.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2017, we launched Active Health as a social movement to encourage Singaporeans to take ownership of their own health and wellness.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, we launched the ActiveSG Circle as a virtual sports centre to continue engaging the public with online classes to get active.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This was something we could do in person physically prior to the pandemic, but we have moved online.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: At MCCY, we recognise the power of sports in bringing Singaporeans together and we will continue to build on these efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Many of our sports businesses and SEPs have also been affected by the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2020, we provided our coaches and fitness instructors with jobs and training opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As at December 2020, SportSG has put together over 400 training courses with a capacity for 8,500 coaches and instructors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In addition, more than 500 temporary jobs have been created through the #SGUnited jobs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we will introduce a new SEP Project Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Like the SEP Grant under the ACRP, this grant supports sports SEPs to collaborate with one another and also other organisations, to develop projects that enhance the health and wellness of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We recognise the important role which many sports freelancers and self-employed persons play, and we want to support you in this endeavour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: One, create more work opportunities for sports Self-employed Persons (SEPs) and freelancers; Two, support capability development through the planning and execution of projects; and Three, support the resumption of sporting and community activities as far as possible.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, we will expand the Enterprise Innovation and Capability Development Grant.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last year, we piloted this at $3 million for the sports industry to build stronger digital capabilities, develop innovative solutions and also, look at how we can upskill.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These initiatives, I must say, are not just reactions to the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we will extend grants to provide continued support for both businesses as well as individuals.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This complements the Jobs Support Scheme which is already in place and which offers wage support for sports operators.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For individuals, we will extend the Training Allowance Grant and the Structured Mentorship Programme till March 2022.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will share more details about our plans to support our sports sectors.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But if you ask any artist or athlete, they will tell you that their true lifeblood is really in performing before an appreciative audience and having a vocal and supportive spectatorship.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And there is something for everyone – whether it is keeping active through online fitness classes, cheering our athletes on, or enjoying a live performance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I urge all of you to support our artists, athletes and instructors as they go on with these performances.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: With the recent move to allow group activities of up to eight persons, community-based teams can take on a four-vs-four format.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Furthermore, we are starting to host international events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last month, we successfully hosted the Singapore Tennis Open, an ATP 250 event.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Over 50 players from more than 15 countries competed, with up to 250 spectators per day allowed in the semi-finals and finals matches.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We showed the world that Singapore can resume international sports events safely.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Looking ahead, we can prepare for the return of more marquee sporting events, such as the Rugby-7s in October.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Mark Chay, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our plans to prepare our athletes in the upcoming games whilst at the same time ensuring their safety.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This year, our athletes can look forward to several Major Games, such as the Olympics, Paralympics, SEA Games and ASEAN Para Games.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We are supporting our athletes’ training while keeping an eye, of course, on the global pandemic situation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes facilitating safe travel for athletes to participate in overseas competitions to qualify for the games, to train and to hone their competitive edge as they prepare to peak at these sporting events.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Singapore Sport Institute and the National Youth Sports Institute specialists are working with our athletes as they resume full training intensity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: As more international qualification competition dates are released, we will schedule our athletes, coaches and officials to be vaccinated progressively.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin and Mr Xie Yao Quan asked about our efforts to provide a safe and positive environment within our sports eco-system.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is a very important issue for us.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: No sportsperson, male or female, should feel unsafe as they train, compete or play in any sports in any role.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The programme will be grounded on three actions – Prevent, Address and Assure.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, to prevent inappropriate behaviour, a Unified Code will be developed to provide the sporting community with a shared reference point against inappropriate behaviour.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have started consultations on the Code with non-government organisations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: And over the next six months, there will be more engagements with athletes, coaches, parents, sport leaders, among others, to refine the Code so that we can achieve a set of standards that will engender confidence in sport participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, to address incidents, a confidential third-party reporting channel and enhanced case management will offer affected individuals access to reporting channels and support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, to assure participants, the Safe Sport Commission will introduce an accreditation framework.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The criteria will be based on the adoption of the Unified Code, implementation of relevant policies and training of persons involved.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Sports organisations that meet the criteria will be accredited through a Safe Sport Mark.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This will help sports participants to easily identify sporting organisations that are committed to practising Safe Sport.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Safe Sport Programme also contributes to the on-going Conversations on Singapore Women’s Development, although not all sport participants are women.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We want to facilitate an on-going and enabling sporting environment that protects both women and girls.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This is also an example of the Government’s approach to addressing women’s development in partnership with stakeholders.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In sports, apart from providing a positive environment and framework for our sporting community, we must also have bold ambitions.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Mark Chay spoke about this, so did Mr Sitoh Yih Pin who asked about our plans to uplift Singapore’s football.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It is the most participated team sport in Singapore, bringing together Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A national team that can perform at the highest level affirms Singapore’s multiple pathways of success and is a source of national pride.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It can also expand opportunities for all – to play, coach or just to be that crazy football fan cheering our team on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our football is not quite where we would like it to be.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We can do more, we can do better, to bring back the Kallang Roar and give our young Lions every opportunity to pursue their dreams.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Chay asked what steps can be taken.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, we will have to grow the base of participation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We have to encourage more to play and give structure to the development of young talent.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our young players spend a lot of their time in school.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must have good coaches and a common system of play with enhanced training infrastructure, wrapped around a football academy for those with the best potential, so that they can train, they can compete and, at the same time, they can continue with their studies.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must also focus on matters off the pitch – areas like fitness, nutrition, discipline and a player's mental fortitude.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All of them are factors which are equally important to success.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But there is one more ingredient for success – and that is our collective will and our collective unity to pursue a shared goal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It has to be all of us, working together, united, pulling in the same direction, for this project to have chance.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Uplifting Singapore football is a national project, and I encourage all of us to rally around our common goal.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will continue to do our best to build a sustainable and resilient football eco-system which Singaporeans can be proud of.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Parliamentary Secretary Eric Chua will share more about these initiatives later on.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Another area of pride and confidence for Singaporeans is our cultural heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our cultural landscape is a rich fusion of traditions, rituals and crafts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are also inextricably bound to each of us and to our own national identity.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We must continue to commemorate and pass it on for future generations.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will redouble our efforts to safeguard both our tangible and intangible heritage and celebrate cultural icons like our Cultural Medallion recipients who have contributed so richly to our nation's development.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Mr Darryl David talked about celebrating our hawker culture, making all of us hungry with his very graphic descriptions of food.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last December, our hawker culture was inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity and I thank everyone for their overwhelming support.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Indeed, we are very, very proud of our hawkers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY and NHB remain committed to promoting our hawker culture.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: First, for the Singapore Heritage Festival 2021, we can look forward to a digital exhibition of poetic and graphical interpretations of our hawker culture.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Second, content related to hawker centre landmarks will be displayed online and at selected MRT stations as part of the "Ride & Discover" exhibition.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Third, we will continue to showcase our hawker culture through festivals, exhibitions and programmes at our museums, using grants from NHB, and taking on board the ideas and suggestions that Mr Darryl David has sketched out.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Twenty-twenty-one marks the 50th anniversary of the promulgation of the Preservation of Monuments Act.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The preservation of national monuments is important to safeguard our heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Our heritage encompasses not only intangible ones like hawker culture, which we spoke about, but also of our heritage buildings.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These structures have withstood the test of time and they very visibly embody our nation's heritage.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We regularly restore our national monuments and we will carry out a series of restoration projects in the coming years to ensure that they continue to stand strong.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Completed restorations include the Abdul Gafoor Mosque, Sultan Mosque and the St James Power Station.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The Istana and Sri Temasek were collectively gazetted as a National Monument in 1992.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: They have borne witness to many historical milestones, including our transition to a sovereign state.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will commemorate the Golden Jubilee of our National Monuments with an exhibition in June 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This exhibition will showcase the preservation journey of all 73 National Monuments for the very first time.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will also be commemorating the 25th anniversary of the Museum Roundtable with a year-long celebration.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: This includes mystery museum tours to explore lesser known museums, a travelling exhibition and complementary museum programmes.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Low Yen Ling, will share more details on these plans.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A key focus of MCCY is our youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Last September, I spoke about how our youths of today will be our leaders of tomorrow.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I know that our young people, especially fresh graduates, at this time, worry that the crisis will have a long-lasting impact on their careers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We understand these concerns and we will do our best to help overcome them.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: My colleague, Minister of State Alvin Tan, will share more about MCCY's efforts to provide opportunities and other pathways for these young people to overcome these challenges and to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Ms Hany Soh and Ms Joan Pereira asked how the Government will encourage more people to care.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: When the pandemic hit, our youths stepped up to help those in need.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Youth Corps Singapore adjusted its volunteering activities to meet community demands.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: For instance, they partnered IMDA to equip seniors with digital literacy skills – very much needed during the digital era of the pandemic – via the Digital Learning Circles.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Youth Corps will continue with these good efforts.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These youths will develop the skills to implement projects to address specific societal needs.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Further, Youth Corps will offer about 4,000 volunteering opportunities for youths.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These include online and, subsequently, physical programmes for persons with disabilities as well.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The responsibility for building a caring society must involve every Singaporean.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: So, on that score, we plan for every town in Singapore to have a coordinating node that brings community groups and resources together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2018, SG Cares Volunteer Centres (VCs) were initiated to achieve this.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: VCs are based in the community, ground-up, chosen to develop and deploy volunteers, foster partnerships – and this includes existing structures that already exist on the ground so that we do not have to reinvent the wheel – and strengthen volunteer management capabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Since end 2018, 12 VCs have been appointed and have engaged about 10,000 volunteers.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: A few weeks ago, the Deputy Prime Minister, Ms Tin Pei Ling and I witnessed the launch of a VC at Geylang town, operated by Care Community Services Society.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In 2016, the Business and IPC Partnership Scheme (BIPS) was introduced to encourage corporate volunteerism.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Through the scheme, businesses enjoy 250% tax deduction on wages and related expenses when their employees volunteer at Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs).

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: The National Volunteer and Philanthropy Centre (NVPC) will lead efforts to raise awareness and also enhance the adoption of BIPS.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: NVPC will introduce a BIPS Clinic for interested corporates to tap into this, to share more and learn more about the scheme.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: MCCY's overarching mission is to bring people together, forging community spirit and intertwining our stories to form a cohesive Singapore Tapestry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That has been the essence and hallmark of everything that we do and all our programmes at MCCY.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: However, for much of 2020, with the pandemic, this was not easy.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: In fact, we had to work on the opposite – keeping people safe meant keeping people apart.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Overnight, many of my Ministry's staff, our partners, our stakeholders and our many community leaders had to pivot to safe management measures and play a variety of different roles to keep Singaporeans safe.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: All of them went the extra mile, well outside their usual comfort zone, to protect the safety of Singaporeans and I thank them very, very much.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: But we also soon realised that being apart did not break us apart.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: It did not dampen our spirits and it did not diminish our desire to keep the threads of our Singapore tapestry strong, cohesive and resilient.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: I am sure that each of us, as I have said earlier, would have our own anecdotes of ordinary Singaporeans doing extraordinary things, going the extra mile, to help one another through this crisis.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: These are the stories that will define us when, one day, we look back and reflect on this crisis of our generation.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: We will remember that, in this crisis, we came out stronger because we went in together.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: That, Sir, is the unfinished story of the Singapore Tapestry.

speaker: The Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
text: Let us continue to weave these stories together and, indeed, we will be stronger as a nation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: (In Mandarin):   Today, I would like to speak on how we can leverage the Chinese media to build up our national image and showcase our soft power so as to promote cultural exchanges.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the 1980s, Singapore developed into an economically prosperous, politically stable and low-unemployment Asian country.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It was then that our cultural life began to flourish.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In the 1980s, xinyao became popular in the various university campuses in Singapore, unleashing a wave of musical creation.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Memories of a generation, changes in the country and society, the living feelings and spiritual outlook of that era were recorded in the form of xinyao.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Emotional interactions were elevated, captured and widely shared through xinyao.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: With the spread of xinyao into other Chinese-speaking societies, Singapore's image gained prominence among other Chinese communities.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Well-known singers such as Stefanie Sun and JJ Lin did not become famous and popular overnight in the Chinese-speaking community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Rather, they became the face of Singapore due to the solid foundation laid down by their predecessors, enabling Singapore to connect with other Chinese-speaking societies through Mandopop.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Besides xinyao, there have been many film and television productions in Singapore in recent years too.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Jack Neo, a talented local director, has made great contributions to the local Chinese film and television scene since the 1990s.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: His film series "I Not Stupid" have become the best-selling movies since independence.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: In addition, in recent years, young directors born in the 1980s such as Anthony Chen and Yeo Siew Hua have also won many awards such as the Golden Horse Award, winning accolades for Singapore art films.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: These films captured the details of our daily lives and our emotional pulse.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: It is this charm that has contributed to the many opportunities for cultural cooperation and exchanges between Singapore and other Chinese-speaking communities, and it is precisely because these films have showcased Singapore's unique multiracial, multi-religious society that audiences in other Chinese-speaking communities were attracted to Singapore.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: This allows us to be more proactive in cultural exchanges between Singapore and other countries in a creative and contemporary manner.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: The growth and spread of Mandopop and films can bring potential economic benefits to Singapore and play a crucial role in building up the country's image and widening its influence among the international Chinese community.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: As the country moves forward, we can document our past from their perspectives, and embrace the future with a stronger sense of identity and existence.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
text: Let us seize the opportunities, strengthen cooperation and work together for a better future.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Consequently, many local arts and culture practitioners were hit swiftly and severely.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Thankfully, many of them were nimble enough to pivot onto the digital platform, applying their creativity in times of adversity.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: As consumers increasingly get used to digital content and experience, digital and blended delivery models will remain relevant post-COVID-19.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: It is, therefore, crucial for the sector to continue developing its digital capabilities to remain competitive.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Such capabilities help local arts and culture products to transcend physical boundaries and reach further.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Picasso said, "Art washes away from the soul the dust of everyday life." We must, therefore, continue to make art available and accessible.

speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
text: Going digital is essential in the new era post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Chairman, COVID-19 has encouraged many arts and culture practitioners to pivot to digital means.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Last April, the Jazz Association here held an online concert, Jass@Home.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: The performance and speakers, including Jeremy Monteiro, had recorded themselves separately and the concert was streamed on the association's FaceBook page and YouTube channel, amongst other platforms.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: I think digital and blended delivery models will continue to be relevant post-COVID-19, although it is still unclear as to where digital art forms would eventually land.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: Some see this as revolutionary, others do not view it as art at all.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: In terms of the art market and its digitalisation, I think blockchain holds some potential in creating a public platform that records and authenticates various transactions.

speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan
text: A possibility is the trading of shares in high value artwork on an online platform, continuously and simultaneously, as a new mode of art investment.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: I recently visited the studio of Mr Lim Tze Peng, a Cultural Medallion recipient.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Mr Lim may be a hundred years old but he never stops reinventing the way he paints.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: His old paintings of shophouses and mama shops brought back fond memories of the corner provision shop that my grandmother used to run in the single-storey shophouses in Princess Elizabeth Estate.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Mr Lim is currently into abstract tree paintings.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: Currently, not enough emphasis is placed on the importance of arts and culture.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: We should use the public spaces and expose people to the different forms and medium of expression of arts and culture.

speaker: Miss Cheng Li Hui
text: We can also have host-schools in constituencies encouraging students from other schools to visit.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, the arts and culture are the soul of Singapore city.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They are integral to our identity, sense of community and well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Year 2020 was a very challenging year for us all.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We want to specially thank all our arts and cultural practitioners for their hard work and perseverance throughout this tough period.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I wish to assure Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, Ms Sylvia Lim, Ms Janet Ang and Miss Cheng Li Hui that MCCY is committed to provide enduring support for the arts and culture sector which plays a critical role in our nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The package also supported over 1,400 digitalisation projects.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since moving into Phase 3, activities in arts and culture are progressively resuming in a safe manner.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: However, we are nowhere, nowhere near pre-COVID-19 levels yet, and we recognise the toll that it has taken on the sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim spoke about safe management measures, or SMMs, and their impact on activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY and the National Arts Council, or NAC, are working closely with MOH and stakeholders to safely resume arts and culture activities, in line with what the public health situation allows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We appreciate that the arts community is keen to have more audiences in their performing arts spaces, but given the global COVID-19 situation, we cannot afford to let our guard down.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Comprehensive vaccination coverage will enable us to re-open further, while SMMs, testing and contract tracing will continue to be necessary.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, our museums can operate at up to 65% capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since Phase 2, arts and culture training classes and workshops have been allowed to resume.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Indoor live performances of up to 250 audience members are presently allowed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: While applications can be made for outdoor performances, live performances that involve unmasked performers carry some risk.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will continue working to expand and restart activities so that our arts practitioners can continue their good work, as we all play our part to ensure a safe and sustainable reopening.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, MCCY is sparing no effort to get the show back on the road and to put jobs back on line.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan would be glad to know the Government has a vigorous slate of additional stimulus and support measures to uplift and uphold this important sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: From fresh funds for operations and new opportunities, to a future roadmap and help to transform – we will reposition this sector for post-pandemic recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Let us elaborate on what Minister Tong has outlined earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This brings our total COVID-19 support to $75 million.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise the contributions many self-employed practitioners, or SEP, have made to our arts and culture sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Due to the COVID-19 restrictions, many of them face uncertainty and loss of income.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last October, I pulled together 12 Government agencies, including colleagues from MOM, MSF, MOE, WSG and SSG to form an inter-agency workgroup tasked to come up with specific ways to boost work opportunities and skills for SEPs in the arts and culture industry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The grant seeks to sustain the livelihoods of freelancers by minimising their job and income loss.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Each project can receive up to $50,000 in funds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The projects can involve live performances, digital presentations or skills development.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We hope this wide-ranging grant, when launched by June 2021, will inject fresh work opportunities for self-employed practitioners and spur them on to create new projects that hone their craft or gear up with skills for a post-COVID-19 recovery.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the impact of the pandemic on arts practitioners, while Ms Janet Ang spoke about helping our artists to enhance their skills and pivot to other sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our creative and technical practitioners are talented and resilient.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The recent Virtual Career Fair organised by NAC and NTUC attracted a total of 27 employers from the arts and adjacent sectors of design, media and education.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: They offered close to 190 job opportunities which drew responses from over 130 applicants.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This positive development reflects the value and continued demand for the skills of freelancers and bodes well for our creative economy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To date, the ACRP has also generated over 5,000 work and training opportunities for SEPs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, there is no returning to the pre-pandemic days and, like many other sectors, the arts and culture industry has to transform and reposition itself for a post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY will introduce a new Business Transformation Fund, or BTF, to equip and enhance the arts and culture sector's capabilities for the future and catalyse its capacity to transform and pivot to new opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Organisations that pool together to explore co-solutioning IT projects that benefit multiple users, or have potential for industry spin-offs can apply for up to $200,000 in funding.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY and NAC will also work with our partners to commission work and co-create business transformation solutions that position arts and culture outfits for the future.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition to these booster shots that gear us up for the new normal, MCCY will also continue to offer relief for daily operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will extend the ACRP Operating Grant to keep arts and culture groups going by helping them to defray operating costs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Year 2020, more than 300 venues were hired under this scheme.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage arts and culture practitioners to take advantage of this subsidy to hold shows, programmes or workshops at the many, many different spaces available.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY will also expand the subsidy to cover more venues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In Mandarin):   To help the arts & heritage sector overcome the challenges arising from COVID, MCCY rolled out the ACRP last year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will also roll out a second tranche of funding for the ACRP Operating Grant to defray operating costs for arts groups.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, we will extend the Venue Hire Subsidy of 80% to June 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: MCCY will also introduce a new Fund to support the transformation of the sector as well as improve the sustainability and development of arts and culture organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: During this period, MCCY hopes to work hand in hand with our partners in the sector to forge forward, find opportunities in this crisis and co-create a creative and prosperous community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: (In English): Chairman, since COVID-19, our arts and culture sector has pivoted towards digitalisation and new ways of engagement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are immensely proud of the resilience and adaptability of our practitioners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Their creative use of technology has brought the arts and culture within the reach of manifold audiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, I saw last month how S.E.A.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Focus reached out to more than 20,000 collectors during the Singapore Art Week 2021; this is multiple times of the physical visitors received.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last October, I met Ms Jayce Tham from CreativesAtWork, who organised the Thriving Singapore virtual exhibition.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is a project supported by the Digital Presentation Grant, or DPG.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The show garnered an online outreach of over 85,000 individuals in just three months.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Digital and blended delivery models will remain the way to go, post-pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: I assure Ms Tin Pei Ling and Mr Xie Yao Quan that digitalisation is and will continue to be a top priority for this sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We will dedicate time and resources to build and enhance digital capabilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Currently, charities in the arts and culture sector can tap on the VWOs-Charities Capability Fund Info-Communications Technology Grant for basic ICT setup and website development and other digital solutions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: In addition, the Charities GoDigital Kit launched last November aims to boost their digital capabilities, especially in corporate and administrative functions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Arts and culture companies, on the other hand, can draw upon the Productivity Solutions Grant, or PSG, and Enterprise Development Grant, or EDG, for the costs of IT solutions and equipment to innovate, upgrade or enhance business processes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We welcome Ms Janet Ang’s suggestion to bring artists and the technology community together to remake innovative models for the arts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This is what we already do and will do more of.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: For instance, National Heritage Board (NHB)’s DigiMuse programme engages the technology sector to enhance the museum experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will provide a framework for the adoption of digital solutions to improve operational productivity and enhance audiences' experiences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The roadmap will be aligned with existing efforts to achieve long-term priority of enhanced digitalisation and technology adoption in the sector, as well as complement new schemes such as the Business Transformation Grant (BTG) that I spoke about earlier.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will also serve as a one-stop directory of relevant government grants and schemes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, even as we pivot towards technology, we remain strongly anchored in our cultural heritage which forms part of our shared identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It reflects who we are and where we come from.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our tangible and intangible heritage reminds us of the progress we have made as a people, and provides us with the foundation to move forward, as a nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: UNESCO’s recognition for our hawker culture speaks volumes of the unique and diverse Singapore heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Mr Darryl David earlier spoke passionately and he hoped for more innovative ways to celebrate our hawker culture as a form of our national pride and legacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We are indeed proud of our cultural assets and want to share these with the world.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To this end, we will widen our search to put other aspects of our cultural heritage for UNESCO nomination.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We invite all Singaporeans to actively contribute their ideas and suggestions to NHB when more details are announced.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, besides food, music and films encapsulate our Singapore culture too.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Earlier on, Mr Sitoh Yih Pin spoke passionately in Mandarin and highlighted the contributions of our local Chinese cultural arts, such as the Xinyao movement and homegrown films.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We recognise how all these various art forms are enriching our growing Singapore identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC has supported new generations of artists like Ms Joanna Dong (董姿彦) and Gen Neo (梁根荣) who are producing fresh Xinyao tunes and contributing to renewed interest in this genre.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Many Singapore films feature covers of Xinyao and Mandarin music.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: A recent collaboration between local band NEKO Highway and director Mr Anthony Chen produced the theme song of his Golden Horse nominated film, Wet Season (热带雨).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, earlier on, Mr Xie Yao Quan asked for greater efforts to enhance our people’s interest and involvement in our arts and culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Allow me to first share how we will foster among Singaporeans a greater appreciation and participation in Singapore’s tangible and intangible heritage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Although the on-going pandemic has changed the dynamics of visitorship, we are pressing on with new plans to draw participation and expanding our audiences through virtual platforms.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Thereafter, the show will travel to other parts of Singapore for the benefit of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: It will feature creative renderings by artists and photographers of all our 73 National Monuments, and include past works that celebrate earlier preservation milestones.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This year is also the 25th Anniversary of our Museum Roundtable, a collective established by NHB to spur a museum-going culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Roundtable has enabled smaller private museums like The Intan, which promotes Peranakan culture, to be heard, which has widened the exchange of insights and views from larger organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: So, to coincide with International Museum Day on 18 May 2021, NHB will launch a series of tours to encourage the public to explore lesser-known museums, and a roving exhibition on the Museum Roundtable will be held in November 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We encourage the public to continue supporting and visiting our museums.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: One of this year’s highlights is the re-opening of the Changi Chapel and Museum (CCM) and Reflections at Bukit Chandu.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: To ensure the continued relevance and accessibility of our museums, we have plans for three heritage centres to be refurbished.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: First, the Malay Heritage Centre will be closed for redevelopment in early 2022.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Its gallery will be updated with new content on the diverse Malay community and Kampong Glam precinct.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Singapore Philatelic Museum that is currently being redeveloped, will reopen next year in 2022 as a dedicated children’s museum with interactive exhibits and storytelling sessions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Come 2023, we can all look forward to a refurbished Peranakan Museum, which will present a more inclusive definition of Peranakan culture.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides rejuvenating our tangible heritage, MCCY will recognise and celebrate the intangible heritage created by our arts and cultural talents, and enhance the public’s appreciation of this legacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: The Cultural Medallion is Singapore’s highest artistic accolade that recognises individuals for their artistic excellence and contributions to our cultural landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: We have many homegrown talents to be proud of.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Since the start of this award, 128 distinguished artists – from the visual and literary arts to music, theatre and dance, across all various arts forms – have won this distinction.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, I met our 2020 Cultural Medallion recipients, Mr Sarkasi Said and Dr Vincent Leow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Like the recipients in past years, they have made a lasting impact on our arts and cultural eco-system.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Last year, NAC engaged over 50 Cultural Medallion recipients on how to better support our arts and culture sector, and as a result the idea of the Cultural Medallion Gallery was born.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Besides the physical exhibits, NAC and the National Library Board will create an integrated and comprehensive national digital repository documenting the work of our Cultural Medallion winners.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: And this will give Singaporeans valuable insights into Singapore’s cultural history.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, Ms Sylvia Lim earlier had asked about the arts fraternity’s response to arts spaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Our arts spaces have grown over the years.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC seeks to ensure that these are used optimally and efficiently; that we provide fair access and inclusive opportunities for as many as possible in the community – especially new groups and younger practitioners; and that these spaces are regularly updated and upgraded to remain relevant to prevailing needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: NAC had conducted extensive consultations ahead of the launch of the Framework for Arts Spaces scheme in year 2010, and Our SG Arts Plan in year 2018.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: This view was also reflected in the Arts Plan.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Chairman, without a doubt, our arts and culture are a source of pride uniting Singaporeans from all walks of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Ms Low Yen Ling)
text: Together, we can turn the corner and bring our arts and culture to higher ground, where talents, creativity and our identity as a Singapore people emerge even stronger.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, they are the unique generation of today, better educated than the previous generation, and more socially connected.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: They have grown up as digital natives with perhaps a different Singapore dream.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Many of the youths of today, perhaps because of their education and exposure through travel and in the social media, are certainly more aware of what is going on; in short, they are more "woke".

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: As seen in recent developments, many are keen to take on causes and stand up for their beliefs, participating avidly in movements and even coming up with their own hashtag causes.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: They are content creators and curators taking to platforms such as TikTok to engage and draw attention to issues.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Yet, due to the way they grew up, they had not necessarily experienced the same hardship and challenges as previous generations, as each generation has typically led a better life than the one before it – until COVID-19 struck.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: COVID-19 has affected this generation like no other.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: It is thus important to have platforms that will allow our youths to give their input to co-conceptualise and co-create the future.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Given that these youths are at home on social media, harnessing these platforms is critical as youths can be encouraged and engaged to co-create solutions for the future.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Even the members of the World Bank-supported Solutions for Youth Employment (S4YE)’s Youth Advisory Group have been using multiple media platforms such as Zoom, Facebook, Twitter and Instagram to highlight the issues and concerns faced by youths to create solutions for the effects of the COVID-19 crisis.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Mr Chairman, aside from this, youths need safe spaces, both emotionally and psychologically, to discuss matters that are important to them, in ways and in language that may be perhaps different from that used by the generations before them.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Some of the issues that are of concern to them could include race, identity, community, health, the environment and religion.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: These safe spaces can be digital ones or physicals ones; but what is important is that there are these spaces to engage in forums or stimulating debates that engage and encourage them to be critical thinkers with diverse perspectives, yet inclusive, helping to reinforce their dignity and self-worth.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: The COVID-19 crisis has also highlighted the importance of transformational change through embracing new ways to build capacity.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Besides these areas, youth may also be involved in areas such as capacity building so that they face the future with real-world skills.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: They can learn as well how to leverage on entrepreneurship and technology to change Singapore, and perhaps the world.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Whether it is co-working areas or start-up incubators that use crowdfunding as a solution to develop ideas, youth projects can be kick-started to allow the young to collaborate with one another or with others.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: To allow more youth to benefit, those with the expertise and interest could help to come up with Kickstarter kits such as tools, both digital and communication-driven, as resources for the incubation of ideas.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Youth advocacy can also be a way in which youths get the opportunity to amplify their voices through carefully thought through ideas on pressing matters that affect their lives today and the future.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: In fact, there is ample evidence from youth engagement efforts abroad that empowering youths can lead to fulfilling intergenerational partnerships.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Young people can engage with society to find purpose and belonging within their own lives.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: Positive emotions are a key resource for people during the coronavirus crisis, according to the University of Melbourne psychology professor Lea Waters in an interview with the Guardian, as they can lead to increased resilience and help in clear thinking.

speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: I hope that the Government can continue to engage our youths and give them the support to emerge from the COVID-19 crisis more resourceful and adaptable, with the right life-skills to succeed in this somewhat uncertain future.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Chairman, COVID-19 has resulted in uncertainty in the job landscape.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: This has affected the vulnerable groups comparatively worse.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: While reaching out to Youth Want Work, a youth employment initiative by Beyond Social Services, I was told that many have started working early to help support the family.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Some as early as 14 years old, while they are still schooling.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: The youths may also be tempted to drop out or not further their education as they may not see the opportunity cost of stopping education while trying to fulfill their immediate needs.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Adam, the lead of Youth Want Work shared, and I quote, “Most youths in this category do mature fast and they do understand the need to better their education but sometimes things at home just doesn't allow them to.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Sometimes, I attribute this notion to the older generation parents, because especially for females, the parents do feel it's better to be married off rather than continuing their studies.” This is something very worrying.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: This pandemic is set to continue for a protracted time.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: It may be difficult for these low-income youths to stop working or to focus on their studies due to their familial financial situation.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: In addition, I understand that the National Jobs Council provides a range of jobs and skills training opportunities for jobseekers under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package and SGUnited Traineeships Programme.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Have employers and such jobseekers expectations and requisite skillsets been met?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Lastly, earlier in February, it was said that there was no available data on the number of youths who take on care-giving duties for elderly family members.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Would the Ministry be able to collect such data, as well as data on whether the youths who have these care-giving responsibilities are able to hold on to promising jobs long term?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: If the number is high, could proactive initiatives be done to reach out to them be considered?

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: Currently, youths are encouraged to reach out only if they require support.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: In this regard, the Ministry may wish to consider partnering with Social Service Agencies that are already working with these low-income youths and thus have better rapport and understanding of them.

speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah
text: They would be well placed to help boost the take up rate of any initiatives introduced and create awareness of applicable national programmes for these youths.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Chairman, one of the ways thus far that MCCY has engaged with our citizens via the Making Stronger Conversations initiative, the platform which operates on a voluntary basis has successfully brought together individuals of diverse backgrounds into conversations to share their ideas and hopes on how to foster a more resilient and inclusive post-COVID-19 society.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: Given how the pandemic has disrupted social relations, such forms of collaborations among citizens as well as partnership between state and citizen have all become more crucial than ever.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman (Marine Parade)
text: How will MCCY continue to provide Singapore from various social groups with not only opportunities to further contribute and develop ideas, but also then translate said ideas into concrete roles and shape the future of Singapore together?

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, Minister Edwin Tong shared how we are forming a cohesive Singapore Tapestry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I will focus on three threads of this tapestry: our youths, our culture of care and our identity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This Thursday, 11 March, will mark one year from the day the World Health Organization declared the COVID-19 outbreak a pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: While no one has been spared from the effects of the pandemic, our youths have felt its impact particularly keenly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They are coming of age into a world which changed, just as they are beginning to make sense of it.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
