text: As one of our youths shared passionately, "COVID-19, you have taken away many conveniences and deprived us of physical contact with our loved ones, but through this adversity you have steeled our resilience, resolve and determination to see to it that we rise above it all." Steeled our resolve.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths are not strawberries in the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They are emerging from the pandemic more resilient and aided in part by the unprecedented support measures by our Government, they have thrived.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The future is uncertain and our youths are asking the question, "What next?" Mr Chairman, I spend plenty of time with our youths this past year and we have wrestled with this question together.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths want good jobs and they want to learn new skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY and NYC are also complementing these national level efforts to help our youths be future ready.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As the hon Darryl David mentioned, youths are digital natives, learning on the fly and keeping a furious pace with and even setting tech trends.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They will apply these skills in the real world, by working on digitalisation projects in organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And our students from Institutes of Higher Learning can join our Youth Corps Internship Scheme (YCIS), to gain work experience in the social and community sectors, develop leadership and project management skills, while giving back to the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, Muhammad Danish, who interned with the Brahm Centre as a volunteer coordinator working on volunteer management and training.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Danish liaised with community partners to match volunteers to their needs, forged friendships with members of the community and gained a deeper understanding of the social service sector.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He has extended his internship with the Brahm Centre while waiting to be enlisted to NS, and he plans to continue volunteering with them.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths can also prepare themselves for the future by broadening their horizons, such as through our Asia-Ready Exposure Programme (AEP), which provides them with short-term overseas exposure opportunities to gain cross-cultural skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But due to COVID-19, AEP has shifted online.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, I urge our youths to take up these opportunities, prepare themselves for the future of work that has arrived sooner than expected due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Dr Shahira Abdullah asked about job-support measures for youths from low-income backgrounds, some of whom may have lost their jobs or may be facing other family issues.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: She also raised concerns over schooling youths who need to work, and youths who have care-giving responsibilities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: I shared how we are helping our youths to prepare themselves for employment.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The initiatives I mentioned earlier are available to all youths, including those from low income backgrounds.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Nonetheless, we recognise that COVID-19 has disproportionately impacted youths from low-income backgrounds, and we are working with our partners to provide more support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, we are strengthening access to mentoring opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We believe that guidance and mentorship can help our youths better navigate challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And so MCCY and NYC partners with youth sector organisations like Access to empower them to make informed career and life decisions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Employment Support Service Providers such as Bettr Barista and YMCA are also providing job matching and placement services, training and support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We also understand that youths with care-giving responsibilities face additional stressors, and are providing them with care-giver, financial and emotional support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For care-giver support, youth caregivers may approach the Agency for Integrated Care (AIC).

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For financial support, they can contact Social Service Officers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For emotional support, they can tap resources such as Fei Yue’s online counselling services.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we are working with these partners to raise awareness of support schemes among our youths.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Youths also care deeply about mental well-being and they want an inclusive and caring society where no one struggles with mental health alone.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This requires a whole-of-society effort, and Parliament Secretary Eric Chua and Minister of State Sun Xueling talked about our Youth Mental Well-being Network, which is key to this effort.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are working with Facebook and TikTok to enhance community support resources on their platforms for users facing distress and using these platforms’ wide reach to foster open conversations and to raise awareness about mental health and cyber wellness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But youths themselves are equally important partners, as they often turn to their friends for peer support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we are exploring more ways to equip more youths with these peer support capabilities, so they can look out for their friends who may be facing mental well-being issues and provide a first line of support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, to help youths identify and navigate the myriad of opportunities available to them, NYC launched Youthopia.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is an online site to provide youths with resources, content and opportunities around jobs and skills, mental well-being and financial literacy.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Youthopia connects youths with coaches for career guidance, or trained professionals and helplines for mental health support.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And we will continue to work with youths and the wider community, so that youths, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds, have opportunities to thrive during and beyond the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths also tell us they want to have a voice and play an active role in shaping their Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: As we work with them to do so, our Government cannot just be here to listen; we must also listen to hear.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Their diversity of ideas is a strength we must respect, cherish and steward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Darryl David and Ms Hany Soh will be pleased to know that we have been stepping up engagements with youths and empowering them to take action on issues that they care about.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are actively engaging youths online where there are so that they can participate, contribute their ideas and share their views.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, in a pre-Budget 2021 conversation that Minister Indranee Rajah and I hosted in January, our youths shared that supporting vulnerable groups is one of the top priorities that our Government should address.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And last year, we engaged youths as part of MHA and MinLaw's review of the sentencing framework for hurt and sexual offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The youths that we spoke to generally agreed that while rehabilitation was an important principle in sentencing, it should not be the dominant consideration in cases involving adult offenders who commit hurt or sexual offences.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MHA and MinLaw took their feedback into consideration and delivered a Ministerial Statement on the outcome of the review here in this House last Friday.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And in our conversations with youths on Singapore Women's Development, they shared that they wanted more support for vulnerable women groups like single mothers or low-income families.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They also raised concerns and aspirations about women-related issues in schools, at homes and the workplaces.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We value their views and will ensure they are considered in the White Paper that will be submitted later this year.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Beyond sharing their views, youths also want to start ground-up initiatives and make a difference in society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are helping them do so with funding, mentorship and connections with industry experts through our Youth Action Challenge, or YAC.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we are working with our youths to turn their ideas and voices, into action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our youths also care about environmental sustainability and they want to address issues like food security and moving towards a zero-waste society.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: They also want to partner us in policy making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We thus started Youth Circles for youth leaders to engage with Government agencies on specific policy issues and to come up with recommendations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, eight members of a Youth Circle with MSE engaged stakeholders on measures to reduce food waste.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And this is really a good example of how our youths are playing an important and impactful part in influencing policy-making.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We are also partnering our youths to shape physical spaces in Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: At our Somerset Belt, groups have put up interactive exhibits and organised physical and digital programmes, such as skate clinics and livestreamed music shows.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will also continue engaging youths to share their ideas for the upcoming youth hub at Kallang where they will get to design a vibrant space to bond and explore interests beyond sports.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, I am really encouraged that our youths are leading the way and showing us how we can collaborate and make a difference.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We can draw from their energy and embody the Singapore Together spirit to shape this place that we call home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And there is no better place to start than to care for one another.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Our culture of care is the heart of what makes Singapore home.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Due to COVID-19, we launched the Emerging Stronger Conversations (ESC) to better understand how our citizens want to deepen this culture of care in the new normal.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Mohammad Fahmi asked about opportunities for Singaporeans to continue contributing ideas and taking action.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: First, as part of the SG Together AfA on Emerging Needs and Volunteerism, citizens prioritised helping seniors gain new skills to help them better navigate a post-COVID 19 landscape.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, RSVP Singapore partnered CapitaLand Hope Foundation and Singapore Pools to establish a "Smart Seniors Applied Learning Centre" to help seniors pick up digital skills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So, we would like to encourage our community partners to join us to design programmes and technology platforms for our seniors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Citizens also recognised how donations-in-kind, such as masks and sanitisers, met community needs in a timely manner at the height of the pandemic.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: For example, Gift for Good, which is a ground-up initiative, created a matching platform to match community resources and community needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: This will give businesses a roadmap to measure their progress and impact as purpose-driven businesses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: But we are only just getting started and there is more to do.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, I will speak in Mandarin, please.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will work with businesses to co-design and co-develop a national blueprint that places purpose, and giving back to society, as the driving forces of a firm besides profit-maximisation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: We will forge forward together, and the Ministry will continue to support more citizen-led efforts and partner all Singaporeans to build a better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: (In English): Mr Chairman, even as we shape the Singapore we want to see, it is also reflecting on our identity as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Like an anchor in a stormy sea, our identity, heritage and history keep us grounded.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: It is also the compass to help us chart our course ahead and key thread in our Singapore tapestry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Last year, a Citizens' Workgroup comprising a diverse group of Singaporeans, explored what it means to be a Singaporean and deliberated on how to refresh content for the Singapore Citizenship Journey, a mandatory induction programme for naturalised citizens.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: MCCY will incorporate the Workgroup's recommendations and our formal response is on our website.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: In May 2020, the National Museum of Singapore launched its Collecting Contemporary Singapore initiative, which will build a collection of objects and stories to remind us of Singapore's history.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: The inaugural theme focuses on COVID-19 and many Singaporeans have responded to the public call for contributions, which is extended now until June 2021.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: And these items will contribute towards content for the Memorial's galleries and gardens, and be used to build up NHB's post-independence history collection.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: Mr Chairman, in the spirit of our Founders' Memorial and as I wrap up my speech about the three traits that weave our Singapore tapestry – our youths, our culture of care and our identity, I thought it apt to quote one of our founders, the late Mr Lee Kuan Yew, whose clarion call 25 years ago resonates even more so today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: He said, and I quote, "To the young and to the not so old, I say, look at that horizon, follow that rainbow, go ride it." In this storm of our generation, all of us, the young and the not so old, are coming together to forge forward and to build a better Singapore.

speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Alvin Tan)
text: So that when this storm finally passes and a rainbow emerges, we will be ready to follow that rainbow and ride it towards the next chapter of our Singapore story.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Chairman, please allow me to take the next four cuts together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: At the outset, I would like to declare that I am Chairman of the SNOC's Athletes' Commission; Member of the Olympic Council of Asian's Athlete Committee; Honorary Secretary of Olympians Singapore and Director of Secretariat at the Global Esports Federation My first cut relates to the development of a skills framework for the sports and fitness industry.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: It is undeniable that for an industry to grow and thrive, it must be set up in an environment that is conducive for such growth.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The necessary conditions must be there to make people to want to join the industry and develop it.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: My question today is, are these conditions present for the sports and fitness industry and can more be done to facilitate this growth?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: To my mind, the industry could do well to develop a framework that is competency and skills oriented.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Countries like the UK and Australia already have frameworks in place that require employers to hire coaches and fitness trainers who complete specified vocational courses.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Further, to get a better sense of the industry's specific needs, the focus should be on engaging the people who do the work daily.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The demands of the industry are everchanging and it would be difficult for the Government machinery to keep pace with the dynamic demands.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: There are many fads out there – the keto diet, Atkins diet, the list goes on.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Would HPB be able to keep coming up with the requisite courses to train people in these areas?

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The short answer is that it would be difficult and costly.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Sports and fitness is a multi-faceted industry and a cookie-cutter approach would be difficult to apply.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: So, considering the industry's needs and the existing infrastructure already in place, I would suggest a skills framework to be developed by the sports industry, for the sports industry, with the full support of the Singapore Government.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: This would lead to a meaningful growth in a more cost-effective and targeted way.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Chairman, my second cut relates to the JSS for the sports and fitness sector.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In my Budget debate speech, I highlighted that the pandemic has severely hit the sports, fitness and wellness industry.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Although Singapore is easing into phase 3, sports and fitness academies and establishments are not able to fully open due to social distancing measures.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Pool space is reduced, school programmes and facilities are limited, and gyms cannot operate to efficient capacities.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Also, establishments located in retail facilities still have the added pressure of rental.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Some gym operators are reporting as low as 50% revenues compared to pre-COVID 19 levels.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I would also like to thank Minister at MCCY for recognising the sector and for extending more support to the industry through the Sports Innovation Grant and Operating Grant extension to December 2021.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: My third cut is on the development of the e-sports industry in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Chairman, it is my pleasure to speak on the emergence and progress of e-sports in Singapore today.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Today, large-scale e-sports tournaments draw more viewers than "traditional sports".

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The world has also come to recognise e-sports as part of the sports eco-system.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: E-sports is one of the sectors which has grown rapidly and accelerated during the pandemic.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: With viewership and gaming participation currently at all-time highs, and in a time where content is king, you can expect e-sports to be here to stay.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The e-sports industry currently sees double-digit growth and such growth has found its way into the Singapore landscape.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: With Singapore's strong local infrastructure, like fast and stable Internet, top global teams have found Singapore very conducive for their professional team training.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: There are more than 20 full-time professional players here, with the top 10 having made more than $3 million in prize winnings alone.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: This figure does not include salaries and sponsorships.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: There are also others employed as full-time coaches and managers of local teams as well as professional teams in major markets like the US and China.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: This will boost many local start-ups and businesses in media, events and supporting services.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Promising local start-ups like yup.gg and EVOS have between them raised more than $31 million in investments and we can expect many more to follow in their footsteps.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: They look on track to follow successful local-born companies like Sea and Razer, who grew a good part of their business thanks to e-sports and gaming, creating thousands of jobs in the process.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Multinational companies in the e-sports and gaming industry like Tencent, Ubisoft and Moonton have also set up regional offices here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: They are expected to introduce hundreds of jobs in the coming year.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: On a sports administrative front, we welcomed the world to the launch of the Global Esports Federation (GEF) on 16 December 2019 to convene the world's e-sports eco-system right here in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: That very same day, we welcomed the world's largest gaming company and technology giant, Tencent, as the founding global partner of the GEF.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Having Tencent with us has helped propel plans into reality.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The GEF launch, watched by over 940 million people across the globe, crystalised in our minds the power, potential and reach of e-sports around the world.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: For us at home in Singapore, we saw opportunities—it is not gaming and e-sports alone but the large, growing eco-system around it.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: The possibilities are boundless across education, events, health and wellness initiatives, technology, artificial intelligence (AI) and innovation.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: With these developments, I believe Singapore can and should do more to take on a leading role in shaping the industry.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Mr Chairman, my remarks today come with a sense of optimism and opportunity, hope, and genuine excitement for the future.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I believe the future of e-sports is incredibly bright if we gather our knowledge, listen to each other and help shape the future together.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: E-sports is alive, it is real and it is evolving at an ever-increasing pace.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Indeed, e-sports can offer a space for everyone and it makes good business and economic sense.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: A rich portfolio of events will fill the calendar with a global platform for competition and entertainment.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: This event offers another excellent opportunity for Singapore to welcome the world and shape how the world consumes live events.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: My sincere hope is that Singapore's e-sports community will grow and prosper and better e-sports globally to benefit athletes, players, teams and other stakeholders in our community.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Just as the Olympic Movement values elevate sports, we hope to highlight and bring out the best in e-sports.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Mr Chairman, my last cut relates to creating our sporting heritage.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: In my Budget debate speech, I took the opportunity to recognise our past athletes who had done Singapore proud in times when resources were scarce and inspired generations after them to take on the mantle and fly Singapore's flag high on the world stage.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Olympians and national athletes in the earlier decades had to resort to their own resources to help sustain and balance earning a living and competing in sports.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: More can be done to recognise and help these athletes who contributed to Singapore's sporting glory and paved the way for future generations to succeed.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I honestly believe that athletes want to continue to give back to their fraternity and inspire Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Indeed, when an athlete retires, there is no engagement beyond that.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Many athletes have gone on to establish themselves in the corporate and business world.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: They would likely hire ex-national athletes and sponsor programmes – they were from the system, after all.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: It is a waste that this is not done.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: My thoughts are that heritage is closely linked with culture.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: Just as we reminisce on the glory of the Kallang Roar, we must remain cognisant that youth today may not know what that means.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: We have a sports heritage in that the current generations can stand on our past sporting giants' shoulders.

speaker: Mr Mark Chay
text: I hope MCCY can do more to recognise and engage past athletes.

speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
text: It was mentioned in one of these articles that there is even a virtual shop space to purchase bookings of public sports facilities such as badminton courts.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Mr Chairman, sports remain an important domain in bringing Singaporeans of all ages together and is also crucial for maintaining our physical and mental wellbeing.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: Last year, MCCY announced the launch of the Children and Youth Sport Framework to provide more opportunities and resources for children and youth to participate in and pursue sports.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: At the Woodlands Swimming Complex, our SportSG's Active Health Coaches and Sport Champions have also been organising aqua-therapy sessions for stroke recovery seniors to improve their mobility as well as their confidence and quality of life.

speaker: Ms Hany Soh
text: How will MCCY continue to create more opportunities for Singaporeans of all ages, including working adults as well as those with mobility issues, to participate in sports?

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has accelerated the push towards digitalisation within most if not all of our sectors, including the non-profit.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: Digitalising becomes especially crucial for organisations that now require new safer means of ensuring continued provision of essential social services to those in need of them within the community.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: The Charities GoDigital kit was also introduced, acting as a comprehensive guide that encourages and aids the digitisation process.

speaker: Mr Mohd Fahmi Aliman
text: How else are we supporting our non-profit sector, of which include charities, to be digitally ready and to thrive in the new normal?

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Chairman, thank you for the opportunity. 2020 was a challenging year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: COVID-19 forced us to change the way we live, work and play.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: What does not change, however, is our commitment to building a caring, cohesive and confident society.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The pandemic brought to the fore the critical role of the People's Association (PA) and I note Mr Leong Mun Wai's related comment.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a Statutory Board, PA's mission is to build up the cohesiveness of our population – a reserve of social capital and goodwill that is built on trust between people and the Government.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is accumulated during peacetime so that we are in a good position when crises – such as the one we are going through right now – hit us.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We did not know when the pandemic would strike.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But when it did, PA swung into action: four nation-wide mask distribution exercises to date; hand sanitiser distribution; food delivery services for the vulnerable, especially during the circuit breaker period; TraceTogether token distribution; and most recently, Community Centres (CCs) operating as community vaccination centres, reaching out to seniors and others to be vaccinated.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A year ago, I am not so sure any of us had "pandemic response" written in our workplans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But the networks, trust and bonds painstakingly built by PA and its volunteers over the years has allowed us to respond cohesively, quickly and as one community during the pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This is the critical difference between our response here in Singapore and the responses we see elsewhere in the world.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To achieve PA's mission, the PA needs to be properly resourced.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And unlike other agencies like IRAS or GovTech, PA manages a whole host of community facilities all across Singapore, fully manned by full-time staff.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These include 108 CCs and 665 Residents' Committee (RC) centres, which need regular maintenance as well as other operating costs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, PA's budget allows it to carry on with its peacetime mission of providing our people with activities – in the thousands every day, actually – that enrich them and which they enjoy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It also enables the building of networks and communities; the relationships of trust.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a former grassroots leader myself – for 15 years, in fact – I am very proud of the work done by PA and its grassroots.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As answered before in this Chamber, the political affiliations of volunteers are not relevant to our consideration in the volunteer's participation in PA because PA's mission is fundamentally focused on community building.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, the social capital that we have built up over time, the harmony that we have and that we enjoy within our society, taking care of our residents, including our seniors and the vulnerable ones amongst us – the value of all these, I would say to this House, is not easily quantifiable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: PA's role in peacetime and in crisis are inseparable.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In many countries, people are quite divorced from the political and administrative machinery.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They have difficulties knowing, much less understanding what goes on.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government is a distant, sometimes even alien, entity.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But in Singapore, we want to explain our policies and provide channels for communication between the Government and the people because we believe the Government must be connected to the people.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Because we believe that nothing can be achieved if we do not get buy-in from our people.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Singapore works only when Government and people, businesses, unions, communities, all come together.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And PA exists to provide the social glue, without which, Singapore would have gotten nowhere.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And the networks and bonds of trust that enable the PA to perform its role in peacetime are also what enable the PA to play a vital role in crises.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: When a major Government policy is announced, PA, together with grassroots advisors, goes to the ground and explains the policies, and that also includes conveying unpopular policies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Hearing directly from residents about their concerns, so that we can actually allow them to voice their concerns, to allow Government to tweak and adapt policies, if needed.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These relationships of trust and comradeship that they have built – bit by bit, through good times and bad – are what enabled us to respond as one Singapore during the pandemic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this is what the late Mr S Rajaratnam meant by a “democracy of deeds”.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, the Member can rest assured that the PA’s budget we have set aside has been put to good use.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And the proof of the pudding is in the eating and there is no doubt that the PA has proven its worth in the past year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Charities play an important role in our society by ensuring no one is left behind.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mohd Fahmi Bin Aliman asked how we are helping our charities to be digitally ready.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Charities can leverage several schemes under this technology hub, including technical advisory, digital implementation consultancy, digital strategy planning, and the adoption of large-scale specialised ICT solutions.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan and Ms Hany Soh asked about how we plan to sustain sports participation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Under our Children and Youth Sport Framework, SportSG is scaling up the Nurture Kids programme in all pre-schools.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are on track to provide all pre-schools with access to the Nurture Kids Train-the-Trainer initiative by 2022.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG is also on track to partner the National Institute of Early Childhood Development (NIEC) to build the capabilities of their lecturers through a co-developed SportSG-NIEC Train-the-Trainer programme.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This will equip early childhood educators with the knowledge to develop children’s fundamental movement skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG’s Active Parents movement has also seen more than 10,000 parents come onboard since the launch in April last year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: During the circuit breaker period, the initiative helped parents stay active with their children through online resources and stay-home virtual activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With the resumption of physical programmes, the Active Parents School Holiday Programme was introduced to provide more opportunities for parent and child to participate in sporting activities together and to encourage parents to take an active role in guiding their child through the activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And I am looking forward to taking part in those activities with my eight-month-old son in time to come.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For working adults, SportSG will launch the Active Health Corporate Playbook in mid-2021.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Playbook guides companies through the principles of health and wellness, organisational development, and evidence-based coaching to help corporates adopt sport and physical activity as an organisational strategy.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: While we have programmes in place, it is also important that we ensure access to our sports facilities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Faisal Manap asked how we are improving our facilities booking system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG actively monitors feedback on the system through channels, such as SportSG’s feedback hotline, the system’s technical helpdesk as well as App Store reviews.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2019, SportSG rolled out version 2.0 of its booking app and regularly releases updates in response to public feedback, as well as to keep up with app developments.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG has also been working to finetune booking policies and stepping up efforts to combat scripting and on-selling activities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, SportSG has enhanced on-site enforcement measures, where hirers of ActiveSG facilities are required to be present or have their booking cancelled.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: It has also enhanced system measures to deter scripting, and imposed stricter penalties against errant members, including account suspension for those found to have abused the system.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Just last month alone, 105 accounts were suspended and 735 bookings cancelled after investigations.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay shared that visitorships at sports and fitness centres have not returned to pre-COVID-19 levels and he suggested that sports and fitness be considered a tier-two sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Since the progressive re-opening of the sports sector in June last year, the sector has benefited from the Sports Resilience Package (SRP) that was launched in October 2020.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Chay may be pleased to note that this year, we will provide more support through the enhancement of the SRP.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This grant helps to defray operating expenses for awardees whose businesses are classified as “Private Academies and Clubs”, “Private League Operators” and “Facility Operators”.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Applicants must show that revenues continue to be severely impacted, show commitment to preserving jobs and must not be receiving other operating grants from the Government, including SportSG.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For coaches, we will extend the training allowance grant and structured mentorship programme to the end of the new financial year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The extended training allowance grant is open to Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents with a valid National Registry of Coaches – or what we affectionately know as NROC – membership who have completed the required training hours based on their membership category.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: With this grant, each NROC coach can claim for continuing coaching education courses, up to a maximum of 30 hours.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Likewise, the structured mentorship programme is also open to all active coaches who are registered with NROC, and coach developers who are Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Projects supported should cover one or more of these categories, and that includes fan or consumer engagement, high performance and sport science, next-generation infrastructure and facilities, or health and wellness.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This grant will give more opportunities for SEPs to work and hone their skills.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The grant for each application is capped at $25,000 or up to 70% of qualifying costs – specifically operating costs for running projects, events or programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG will also support the industry through an Industry Development Plan that sharpens our approach to growing the sports sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The plan will support the sector in adapting and innovating through the enhancement of digital capabilities and innovation.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG will also develop a digitalisation roadmap to help businesses assess digital readiness, identify innovation and opportunities, and spur digital adoption.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The second area is the enhancement of workforce capabilities that will see collaborations between workforce and educational agencies to develop a skills framework.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this will help provide better careers, training, education and professional development pathways for the sports workforce.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Currently, CoachSG works closely with educational institutions, such as Republic Polytechnic, the National Institute of Education, Nanyang Technological University, and has strong partnerships with overseas organisations to develop capabilities and content.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: There are also partnerships with industry players, such as NTUC’s National Instructors and Coaches' Association, to provide coaches and fitness instructors with opportunities for professionalisation and career development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Mark Chay also suggested developing the e-sport industry and community in Singapore.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: MCCY and SportSG have, indeed, been working with the relevant Government agencies to explore opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, agencies have been supporting major e-sports events, local start-ups, as well as building the talent pipeline for the video games industry.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This includes the Global Esports games where SportSG has been engaging the organisers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are also supporting the building of an e-sports community, especially among the youth through community events, community sports clubs, NYC and *SCAPE.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: At the same time, MCCY is working with MSF and NYC and a panel of youth on guarding against potential ill effects of e-sports.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG is also working with stakeholders to put together a code of practice.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: For instance, SportSG will be working with MOE to have all Primary and Secondary school students educated on the risks associated with gaming through cyber wellness education resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie Yao Quan asked how our athletes are preparing for the Major Games.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Xie also shared that that our athletes need to be supported to embrace challenges in the “new normal”.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are working closely with the Tokyo Olympics Games Organising Committee to ensure the safety of our athletes and officials.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This includes a COVID-19 testing regime and allowing accredited athletes to train during the 14-day quarantine period, subject to a negative swab test.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our swimming and badminton teams are also looking forward to a Pre-Games Training Camp in July in Kochi, Japan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And this is made possible by an MOU between SportSG and the Kochi Prefectural Government.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This system will be piloted in three sports – swimming, table tennis, football – and will be deployed at selected venues.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The first batch of cameras for swimming has already been installed at the Singapore Sports School and will be rolled out across the two other sports within the year.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Besides empowering our active athletes, I thank Mr Mark Chay for his suggestion to set up an alumni for Team Singapore and we are happy to explore this further.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Currently, Team Singapore athletes who have represented Singapore at the Major Games are granted free lifetime access to ActiveSG swimming pools and gyms and invited to attend sports events.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Those who have been inducted into the Sports Hall of Fame are also given additional access to sports medicine services at the Singapore Sports Institute Sports Medicine Centre and are invited to speaking engagements at schools and sports clinics.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: SportSG will continue to work with key stakeholders, such as the Singapore National Olympic Council (SNOC), the Singapore National Paralympic Council as well as the National Sports Associations (NSAs), to proactively engage these athletes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have not been doing well in football in recent years.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a teenager, I was neither a good footballer, nor was I a most diehard fan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: But I could, like many in my generation, rattle off names of football heroes that everyone knew: Fandi Ahmad, Nasri Nasir, Lim Tong Hai and super sub Steven Tan.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And who could forget legendary bicycle kick goal that Sundramoorthy scored against Brunei in 1993!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The electricity was in the air at that point in time – in the Kallang Stadium, in the coffee shops, in our homes, in front of our TV screens.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Each time Singapore's team scored a goal, our entire neighbourhoods would shake with excitement and passion and we rallied behind our football teams.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: So, this is my plea, not just to Members of this Chamber, but to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Whatever your views of the state of football right now, I ask for your support as we reimagine and re-energise Singapore football.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will start with our children and youth.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Talented students outside these SFAs will also be scouted to join the ActiveSG Football Academy Development Centres so that they too, can receive similar levels of training support and competition exposure.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: FAS is in discussions with overseas football institutions such as La Liga, Bundesliga Club Borussia Dortmund as well as Australian colleges such as Maribyrnong College.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Locally, we will work with clubs such as the Lion City Sailors to provide similar opportunities.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our footballers will be tracked through a national athlete monitoring database, which will operate alongside a new Football High Performance Centre, that brings together our sport science capabilities under a technology-enabled space.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will also work with our partners to improve the ecosystem.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: One example is the provision of NS support for our elite and aspiring footballers.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: These are just some examples of what we are doing.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: More details will be announced by FAS and SportSG in due time.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Chairman, I would like to declare at this point that I am not citing this next quote because of your allegiance to a certain football club but because I truly believe in what has been said.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Liverpool legend Bill Shankly once said, and I quote, "if you cannot support us when we lose or draw, don't support us when we win." Members of this Chamber, deep down in our hearts, I know Singaporeans are not fair-weathered fans.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Whether we are supporting our footballers, our athletes at the Olympics or the SEA Games, let us all stand resolutely behind our athletes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: They have poured blood, sweat and tears into their sport, made sacrifices to be the best they can be, so let us all, as fans of Team Singapore, give them our wholehearted support!

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Chairman, to conclude, whether it is about supporting our fellow men and women in our charities, sports, arts, youth or community sectors, Singapore can be a caring, cohesive and confident society only if we continue to weave our diverse threads together, as one Singapore tapestry.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Chairman, I have clarifications for Minister of State Low Yen Ling who responded to my cut on the art spacers.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: That is the first question, whether Government sees value in centres being managed by artists rather than the Government all the time.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Second clarification is, she mentioned that there were many dialogues between the arts community and the National Arts Council (NAC), and the principle that arts venues needed to be as accessible to as many practitioners as possible.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: It does not have to be something managed by the NAC.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: My final clarification is regarding the consultation between the Government and the arts community.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I would like to ask whether the Government would look into assessing whether the current dialogue formats can be improved, so as to convince, I suppose, the Arts community that their concerns are being taken seriously, and that the Government is coming with an open mind to these discussions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Chairman, I want to thank the Member Ms Sylvia Lim for her clarifications.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: And I want to use this opportunity to reiterate that the Government is committed to helping our arts and culture sector to recover from the disruptions of the pandemic to transform, to future-proof ourselves, and also to thrive in the new normal of the post-COVID-19 world.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I had spent some time to outline the various new measures, the top up to ACRP, and not just the operating grant but the venue hire subsidy and also the SEP grant and so on; to demonstrate the Government's commitment to turbo-charge and turbo-boost our arts and culture sector.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To her three clarifications, besides the various funding, I talked about another key means of support for the arts and culture sector is the provision of infrastructure.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, the extension of the venue hire subsidy with the enhanced ACRP really serves to defray costs, improve cost recovery and also encourage more shows and activities to be conducted.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Earlier on, I explained that in land scarce Singapore, we have a responsibility to ensure that the space is used optimally and effectively.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We seek to provide fair access and inclusive opportunities for as many as possible in the community, especially new groups and young practitioners, who need that incubator space.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: It is also our aim to ensure that the spaces are regularly updated, regularly upgraded to stay relevant to prevailing needs and to serve the overriding goals of the arts and culture community.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I also want to use this opportunity explain that NAC takes a calibrated approach to spaces as well as grants.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: For example, where they are providing specific project grants – because after all, this is taxpayers' money – or even managing the Arts Resource Hub co-working space, they will exercise greater oversight.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: But otherwise, NAC will provide recipients with the autonomy to utilise and maximise the resources that they are accorded within mutually agreed conditions.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Allow me to use this opportunity to update some numbers.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: To Ms Lim's point about The Substation, allow me to use this opportunity to share that MCCY and NAC recognise the contributions which The Substation has made to our arts and culture landscape over the past 30 years.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: I have attended many such programmes in my teens and early 20s.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We had hoped that The Substation would continue its role as an arts incubator.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Since 2017, NAC has proactively engaged The Substation and offered support in various, various ways, in different permutations and scenarios.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Following the renovation, which was already scheduled a few years ahead of time, we hope that the place will continue to support the work of young and unproven practitioners and be a haven for collaboration and the arts and culture community.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We want to use these few months to conduct focus group discussions with the various stakeholders, freelancers, arts and culture organisations and so on, to take in the views, to scope out the various grants.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: We will also similarly, take the same consultation approach with regards to infrastructure and art space.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Just to pick up on the point by hon Member Ms Sylvia Lim.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I took a walk down to 45 Armenian Street yesterday just to understand the situation better.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I noticed that 45 Armenian Street is located in the heart of the city and actually surrounding it are many arts groups, such as School of the Arts, LASALLE College of the Arts, NAFA and SMU is just next door.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: In my mind, our friends in the arts fraternity, are a group of people who possess the unique ability to turn black and white, into a rainbow of colours.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: So, in that context, I would like to ask Minister Edwin Tong, what is the strategy and philosophy to support our arts group and in the context of 45 Armenian Street, after the renovations, would more arts groups be able to benefit from the use of that space?

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: This discussion with The Substation started more than two years ago.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: And users, such as The Substation, was, in fact, invited back; they will be part of the multi-tenants, and they will have access to all of the renovated facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: So, that was the thinking behind Armenian Street.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In relation to the various models that, I think, Ms Lim also spoke about earlier, there are many which are run by arts companies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: TheatreWorks, for instance, is one; Objectifs is another.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: But, equally, I will say that in Singapore, we have a model which has a mix of different types of management systems and operating models.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: We have those which are run by their own arts companies.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: Equally, we have those which are run on the basis of shared facilities and they have done well, like Nine Years Theatre, like Pangdemonium, as examples.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: These have done well, even though they have shared facilities.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: In the context of looking at how we rationalise the space, my colleague Minister of State Low has spoken earlier.

speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
text: The objective is to ensure that spaces remain available for experimentation, for incubation, for community uses and, ultimately, have a safe space for artists to continue to express themselves.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin, would you like to withdraw your amendment, please?

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: Mr Chairman, I thank all Members for their COS cuts.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: I also like to thank the MCCY team for their great effort and responses.

speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
text: With that, Mr Chairman, I beg leave to withdraw my amendment.
